latestRelease.notes:
# Agent

### Prelude

Released on: 2026-08-11

- Please refer to the [7.82.1 tag on integrations-core](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/master/AGENT_CHANGELOG.md#datadog-agent-version-7821) for the list of changes on the Core Checks

### Bug Fixes

- Windows: Fixed an issue where an explicit `DDAGENTUSER_KEEP_RIGHTS` or `DDAGENTUSER_NAME` value passed as an install argument to a Fleet Automation-triggered Windows Agent install/upgrade could be silently overridden by a stale fallback value (respectively from the registry and from the running service account).
- Fix an issue where GPU monitoring could trigger a kernel panic on multi-GPU nodes with Hopper/Blackwell GPUs.

signals.title: [BUG] `pkg/util/log`: test-only helpers use a non-standard `//go:build test` tag instead of `_test.go` naming
signals.text: ### Agent version v0.82.0 ### Bug Report ### Summary Several files in `pkg/util/log` (and its `slog`, `slog/formatters`, `slog/handlers`, and transitively `zap` subpackages) gate test-helper code behind a custom `//go:build test` constraint instead of using the standard Go convention of a `_test.go` filename suffix: - `pkg/util/log/logger_test_utils.go` - `pkg/util/log/log_test_init.go` - `pkg/util/log/slog/logger_test_utils.go` - `pkg/util/log/slog/formatters/template.go` - `pkg/util/log/slog/handlers/test_utils.go` These define symbols (`LoggerFromWriterWithMinLevelAndLvlFuncMsgFormat`, `LoggerFromWriterWithMinLevelAndLvlFuncCtxMsgFormat`, `Template`, `newMockInnerHandler`, etc.) that real `_test.go` files in the same packages reference unconditionally — including `log_test.go`, `log_bench_test.go`, `klog_redirect_test.go`, `wrapper_test.go`, `pkg/util/log/slog/formatters/template_test.go`, `pkg/util/log/slog/handlers/async_test.go`, and (transitively, via `slog.LoggerFromWriterWithMinLevelAndFormat`) `pkg/util/log/zap/zapcore_test.go`. Inside this repo, the gap is invisible: `dda inv test` and this repo's own Bazel setup (`bazel/rules/go/dd_agent_go_test.bzl`'s `dd_agent_go_test` macro) both know to add `"test"` to the build tags for test targets — `UNIT_TEST_TAGS`/`BASE_TEST_TAGS` in `tasks/build_tags.bzl` include it — while production targets (`dd_agent_go_binary`, using `COMMON_TAGS`) deliberately don't. Because rules_go's `gotags` attribute is a per-target build configuration transition rather than a global flag, the *same* `go_library` (e.g. `pkg/util/log/BUILD.bazel`, which already lists these files as `go_library` srcs, not `go_test` srcs) compiles differently depending on whether it's pulled in by a test target or a production binary target. So within this repo's own tooling, everything works, and `log_test_init.go`'s `init()` never reaches a production binary. That safety net only exists because of this repo's custom macros. It disappears the moment `pkg/util/log` is consumed the normal way: as a versioned Go module (`go get github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pkg/util/log`, currently tagged through `v0.82.1`) built with stock `go build`/`go test`/`go vet`/`golangci-lint`, or with a plain Gazelle setup that has no equivalent of `dd_agent_go_test`'s tag wiring. Such tooling has no way to know it needs `-tags test`, so: 1. **Its own tests on this package fail to compile** — `go vet`/`go test` on `pkg/util/log` (and `slog`, `slog/formatters`, `slog/handlers`, `zap`) hit undefined-symbol errors, since the helper files aren't visible without the tag. 2. **If it "fixes" that by adding `-tags test` globally** (the only lever a plain Go/Gazelle consumer has, lacking per-target transitions), `log_test_init.go`'s `init()` — which reads `DD_LOG_LEVEL` from the environment and overrides the configured log level — now compiles into that consumer's production build too, silently making log level overridable via an environment variable outside of tests. ### Expected behavior Test-only helper code should either: - be named with a `_test.go` suffix (works everywhere, no tooling needs to guess — true for `log_test_init.go` and `slog/handlers/test_utils.go`, which appear to only be needed by the package's own tests), or - if it must be importable by external test packages (the presumed reason it isn't `_test.go` today — non-`_test.go` files can be imported as a normal package dependency, `_test.go` files cannot — likely true for `logger_test_utils.go`, `slog/logger_test_utils.go`, and `slog/formatters/template.go`), be moved to a clearly-separated, explicitly-imported subpackage (e.g. `pkg/util/log/logtest`) rather than gated by an ad hoc build tag inside the main package. Either fix removes the need for any external consumer to guess at and pass `-tags test`, and removes the risk of test-only code (especially `log_test_init.go`'s env-driven `init()`) being pulled into a production build by a consumer that doesn't have this repo's Bazel per-target tag scoping. ### Affected version Present on `main` as of 2026-08-18 (`pkg/util/log` currently tagged through `v0.82.1`, with `v0.83.0`/`v0.84.0` in pre-release/devel). Introduced by #42856 (2025-11-07); not present before that PR. ### Suggested fix Rename the non-`_test.go` files gated by `//go:build test` to end in `_test.go` where they're only ever needed by the package's own tests, or split the cross-package-importable helpers into a dedicated `logtest`-style subpackage. ### Reproduction Steps ``` $ cd pkg/util/log $ go build ./... # succeeds — production code is unaffected $ go vet ./... # fails: slog/formatters/template_test.go:22:15: undefined: Template slog/handlers/async_test.go:23:11: undefined: newMockInnerHandler klog_redirect_test.go:27:10: undefined: LoggerFromWriterWithMinLevelAndLvlFuncMsgFormat zap/zapcore_test.go:113:19: undefined: slog.LoggerFromWriterWithMinLevelAndFormat $ go test ./... # same undefined-symbol failures across pkg/util/log, # pkg/util/log/slog/handlers, pkg/util/log/slog/formatters ``` This pattern was introduced deliberately (see #42856, "Move Default log function behind test build tag", merged 2025-11-07) to keep a bare stdout logger (`Default()`) out of production binaries — so any fix needs to preserve that intent, not just revert it. ### Agent configuration _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Other environment details _No response_

signals.title: feat(ksm): add kube-state-metrics NetworkPolicy support
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds first-class support in the `kubernetes_state_core` check for kube-state-metrics NetworkPolicy metrics: maps `kube_networkpolicy_spec_ingress_rules` and `kube_networkpolicy_spec_egress_rules` to Datadog metrics, maps the `networkpolicy` label to `kube_networkpolicy`, adds default label joins from `kube_networkpolicy_labels` (standard Datadog / Kubernetes / Helm labels), and adds a `kubernetes_state.networkpolicy.count` aggregator by namespace (aligned with other namespaced resources such as ingress). ### Motivation NetworkPolicy metrics are exposed by kube-state-metrics but were not translated or enriched like other resources, so they were ignored by the check. ### Describe how you validated your changes Ran `go test -tags='kubeapiserver test' ./pkg/collector/corechecks/cluster/ksm/... -short`. ### Additional Notes Upstream KSM already includes `networkpolicies` in default collectors; this change focuses on Datadog metric naming, tagging, label joins, aggregation, and tests. **Risk:** None

signals.title: add eviction configs
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Pick up NCM eviction configurations from the datadog.yaml. Use these values in the eviction function. Call the eviction function after we write to the db to ensure that we do not exceed memory constraints. Evictions are tracked under a new Datadog internal metric: `datadog.ncm.store.configs_evicted` ### Motivation ### Describe how you validated your changes ### Additional Notes ### Local Validation That datadog.yaml is read correctly set `dev/dist/datadog.yaml`: ``` log_level: debug api_key: *** dd_url: 'https://dd.datad0g.com/' hostname: "sophie-local" process_config: process_collection: enabled: true network_devices: config_management: rollback: enabled: true store: min_configs_per_device: 2 max_configs_per_device: 24 max_raw_config_store_bytes: 2000000000 ``` run commands: ``` dda inv agent.build --build-exclude=systemd ./bin/agent/agent run -c ./bin/agent/dist/datadog.yaml ``` View debug logs: ### CML eviction e2e test Confirmed eviction order with simulation on CML - set low number of bytes for store config - change configuration of network device, expecting removal of configurations in alignment with eviction policy - check evicted uuids in logs, confirm that inventory_reported_at does not continue to update for evicted configs in orgstore ### QA flow in CML 1) Configure datadog.yaml file inside of CML yaml file for test case, import lab to CML 2) Make needed configuration changes for test case 3) Validate Boltdb state with the following steps: ssh into vm running agent in cml, display device_config.db in cml as base 64: `sudo base64 /opt/datadog-agent/run/ncm_config.db` copy and paste the db output into a .txt file in local computer convert to a bin file: `base64 -d ~/Documents/cml_boltdb.txt > ~/Documents/cml_boltdb.bin` explore file using ncm show: ``` cd ~/go/src/github.com/DataDog/ndm-tools/ncmshow ./ncmshow ~Documents/cml_boltdb.bin ``` ### Manual test cases 1) Set configuration to: min_configs_per_device: 1, max_configs_per_device: 24, max_raw_config_store_bytes: 8 Get BoltDB state: Change hostname Get BoltDB state: (Should see 2 configs per device, even though min configs is set to 1 it should get overridden to 2. Min configs should override the config store requirement - will see that even after eviction not within this setting.) - note here, old running config was evicted so that the modified one could be stored 2) Set configuration to: min_configs_per_device: 1, max_configs_per_device: 3, max_raw_config_store_bytes: 1000000 Change hostname Change hostname Get BoltDB state: BoltDB only has 3 max configs for evictionCML2:10:10:1:2 even though there is enough space in the (db only 66000 bytes) because of the upper max_raw setting.

signals.title: feat(serverless-init): add shared infrastructure for AWS MicroVM cloud service
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds the shared Go infrastructure that AWS MicroVM cloud-service support depends on. This is the first in a stack of PRs that together deliver full MicroVM observability. ### Motivation The Datadog Agent's serverless-init supports multiple cloud platforms (Cloud Run, Container Apps, etc.) via a `CloudService` abstraction. AWS Lambda MicroVMs are a new deployment target where the Agent runs as an init process inside a Firecracker microVM. Each new platform requires small additions in a few central places before the platform-specific code can be wired in cleanly. This PR makes those additions in isolation so the platform-specific MicroVM PR is a clean diff: - **`pkg/metrics/metricsource.go`** — adds `MetricSourceAWSMicroVMEnhanced`, the metric source tag used on all MicroVM enhanced metrics. - **`pkg/serverless/env/env.go`** — adds `MicroVMImageARNEnvVar` (`AWS_LAMBDA_MICROVM_IMAGE_ARN`), the env var the platform injects with the image ARN. - **`pkg/serializer/internal/metrics/origin_mapping.go`** — maps the new MetricSource to its origin string so metrics are routed correctly in the serializer. - **`comp/dogstatsd/server/impl/default_serverless.go` + `enrich.go`** — threads MicroVM origin/tag enrichment through DogStatsD's serverless path. - **`comp/logs-library/processor/json_serverless_init.go`** — adds a JSON log encoder for structured serverless-init logs, needed for MicroVM's log pipeline. ### Describe how you validated your changes - New unit tests cover the origin mapping and DogStatsD enrichment paths. - All changes are additive; no existing behaviour is altered. Run the unit tests for the packages touched by this PR: ``` dda inv test --targets=./comp/dogstatsd/server/impl,./comp/logs-library/processor,./pkg/metrics,./pkg/serializer/internal/metrics,./pkg/serverless/env ``` ### Additional Notes **PR stack** (each PR bases on the one above): 1. **This PR** — shared infrastructure 2. `microvm-02-cloudservice-run` — `Run()` method on `CloudService` interface 3. `microvm-03-lifecycle-config-childhandle` — lifecycle package primitives 4. `microvm-04-lifecycle-forwarder` — HTTP pass-through proxy 5. `microvm-05-lifecycle-heartbeat` — periodic heartbeat metric 6. `microvm-06-lifecycle-server-wire` — lifecycle HTTP server 7. `microvm-07-microvm-service-wiring` — MicroVM `CloudService` + main wiring 8. `microvm-08-sigusr2-on-run` — SIGUSR2 on `/run` for PRNG reseeding

signals.title: feat(serverless-init): add standalone MicroVM lifecycle HTTP server
signals.text: ## Summary This adds the MicroVM lifecycle HTTP server itself: an `http.Server` listening on the configured port, handling the six lifecycle hooks the AWS MicroVM platform sends — `/ready`, `/validate`, `/run`, `/resume`, `/suspend`, and `/terminate` — in **standalone** mode, i.e. the agent answers each hook itself rather than forwarding it to a user application (that pass-through mode is added later in this stack). The motivation is to give the agent visibility into a MicroVM's full lifecycle without requiring any cooperation from the user's own application: `/ready` reports child-process liveness so the platform knows when it's safe to snapshot; `/run`/`/resume`/`/suspend`/`/terminate` each emit an enhanced lifecycle metric (tagged with the MicroVM instance ID once known), and `/suspend`/`/terminate` additionally flush all pending telemetry (metrics, traces, logs) before responding, since those are the two points where telemetry could otherwise be lost — either frozen into a snapshot or torn down with the VM. `/run`'s request body (the `runHookPayload` a caller passes to `RunMicrovm`) is capped at **1 MiB** via `http.MaxBytesReader` before being buffered; a body exceeding the cap, or any other read error, aborts the handler with a 500 rather than silently forwarding a truncated body. This cap is a self-imposed defensive bound, not a value taken from an AWS-published limit — the AWS Lambda MicroVM reference docs describe `runHookPayload` only qualitatively (tenant IDs, signed URLs, secret references) and state no numeric size limit. ## Stack This is **PR 2 of 4** in a split of https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53035 ("feat(serverless-init): add MicroVM lifecycle HTTP server and env-var wiring"), which was too large to review as a single PR. The full stack, in merge order: 1. wire MicroVM lifecycle server config from env vars 2. **(this PR)** add standalone MicroVM lifecycle HTTP server 3. propagate MicroVM ID to logs and trace tags 4. add MicroVM lifecycle user-app forwarder pass-through The tip of PR 4 is byte-for-byte identical to the original `tianning.li/microvm-06-lifecycle-server-wire` branch. Note: this PR is somewhat larger than the ~300-line target used elsewhere in the stack — the server skeleton (types, `NewServer`, all six handlers, the shared flush path) is a single cohesive, self-contained unit and its test suite cannot be meaningfully subdivided without breaking that self-containment. ## Test plan ``` bazel test //cmd/serverless-init/lifecycle:lifecycle_test ``` - [x] `bazel build //cmd/serverless-init/lifecycle:lifecycle` - [x] `bazel test //cmd/serverless-init/lifecycle:lifecycle_test` - [x] `dda inv linter.go --targets=./cmd/serverless-init/lifecycle` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: feat(serverless-init): add ProcessHooks for subprocess liveness tracking
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a `*ProcessHooks` parameter (`OnAlive`/`OnDead`) to `mode.RunInit` and its internal `execute()`, so a caller can be notified when the spawned user process starts and exits. `mode.Conf.Runner` is dropped for init-container mode — its field type (`func(*serverlessLog.Config) error`) can no longer match `RunInit`'s new two-argument signature, so `main.go` switches from calling `modeConf.Runner(logConfig)` to `cloudService.Run(modeConf, logConfig)`, which already exists on the `CloudService` interface and produces identical behavior for every existing cloud service (sidecar → `RunSidecar`, init-container → `RunInit` with `nil` hooks). Also adds `cloudservice.MicroVM`, a `CloudService` implementation for AWS Lambda MicroVMs, and a `LifecycleContext` type carried on `TracingContext.LifecycleCtx`: - `GetTags` parses `DD_AWS_MICROVM_IMAGE_ARN` for `region`/`account_id`/`image_name` (falling back to `"unknown"` for any field it can't parse). - `GetEnhancedMetricTags` derives base/usage tag sets from those tags. - `Init` reads a `LifecycleContext` (metric/log flushers, trace-tag/log-tag setters, flush timeout, sidecar flag) and constructs + starts the lifecycle hook server. - `Run` spawns the user process via `mode.RunInit`, binding `ProcessHooks.OnAlive`/`OnDead` to the lifecycle server's child so its `/ready` check reflects real liveness. Sidecar mode is fatal for MicroVM — there's no child process to track, so `/ready` would silently return 503 forever instead of surfacing the misconfiguration. - `Shutdown` stops the lifecycle server within a bounded timeout so in-flight `/suspend`/`/terminate` requests can complete before the metric/trace agents tear down. - MicroVM supports both amd64 and arm64 (every other cloud service here is amd64-only). `MicroVM` is **not yet reachable**: `GetCloudServiceType` still doesn't know about it, so nothing in the running agent changes yet. Also fixes review feedback from Copilot on this PR: - `mode/initcontainer_mode.go`: `hooks.OnDead`'s defer was registered only inside the `hooks.OnAlive != nil` branch, and after `OnAlive()` ran. An `OnDead`-only hook never fired, and `OnDead` wouldn't fire if `OnAlive` panicked. Now deferred unconditionally right after `cmd.Start()` succeeds. - `main.go`: fixed a non-gofmt-compliant import grouping. - `cloudservice/microvm_test.go`: reworded stale `/launch` references (test names, a path variable, assertion messages) to `/run`, matching the route actually under test. ### Motivation The upcoming MicroVM `CloudService` needs to know whether the customer's process is currently alive so its lifecycle server can answer `/ready` correctly — there's no other signal available once `cmd.Start`/`cmd.Wait` are called deep inside `mode.execute()`. `ProcessHooks` is the minimal hook point for that. `MicroVM` is the core piece of the MicroVM integration: everything needed to answer the lifecycle server's HTTP hooks and track the user process's liveness, in one type that satisfies `CloudService` end-to-end. This is the split of #53036 (`tianning.li/microvm-07-microvm-service-wiring`). Originally planned as 5 independently-reviewable PRs; PR 2 (MicroVM CloudService implementation) has since been merged into this branch, so **this PR now covers PRs 1 and 2 combined**: 1. ~~ProcessHooks plumbing in `mode` package~~ (this PR) 2. ~~MicroVM CloudService implementation (`cloudservice/microvm.go`)~~ (this PR) 3. MicroVM tags/metrics/arch tests 4. MicroVM lifecycle-server tests 5. main.go wiring + CloudService registration (tip == original #53036) ### Describe how you validated your changes ``` dda inv test --targets=./cmd/serverless-init/... ``` 299 tests pass (4 platform-skips). New coverage: - `initcontainer_mode_test.go` pins `OnAlive`/`OnDead` ordering (start → alive → wait → dead), the nil-hooks no-op path, `Conf.Runner` nil-for-init/non-nil-for-sidecar, and two regression tests for the OnDead/OnAlive fix above (`TestExecute_OnDeadOnly_OnAliveNil_StillFires`, `TestExecute_OnAlivePanics_OnDeadStillFires` — both fail against the pre-fix code). - `mode_windows_test.go` covers the updated stub signature. - `cloudservice/microvm_test.go` and `cloudservice/service_test.go` cover `MicroVM`'s tag parsing, enhanced-metric tags, init/run/shutdown, and selection priority over Cloud Run. ### Additional Notes No `BUILD.bazel` changes needed — `cloudservice/`, `mode/`, and `cmd/serverless-init/*.go` are Gazelle-excluded (see root `BUILD.bazel` lines 97-100).

signals.title: fix(serverless-init): eliminate GlobalTags data race in MicroVM trace tags
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Stops MicroVM's async `/run` lifecycle hook from mutating `Agent.GlobalTags` and routes the dynamic `lambda_microvm_id` tag update through the (already serverless-owned) span modifier instead. Concretely: - `pkg/serverless/trace/span_modifier.go`: `tags` field is now `atomic.Pointer[map[string]string]` (using `go.uber.org/atomic`, per repo convention); `ModifySpan` applies each tag lock-free via `Load()`. - `pkg/serverless/trace/trace.go`: adds `UpdateRuntimeTags`, which updates only the span modifier — never `GlobalTags`. The existing `SetTags` (called once, synchronously, at startup before the trace agent runs) is untouched and still updates both. - `cmd/serverless-init/main.go`: the two async `TraceTagSetterFunc` closures wired into the MicroVM lifecycle server now call `UpdateRuntimeTags` instead of `SetTags`. - `cmd/serverless-init/lifecycle/server.go`: updated a doc comment that named the (now stale) method satisfying `TraceTagSetter`. ### Motivation Codex flagged a data race on #53036: `serverlessTraceAgent.SetTags` is invoked from a goroutine inside the MicroVM lifecycle server's `/run` handler, which runs concurrently with the trace agent's span-processing loop. `SetTags` calls `Agent.SetGlobalTagsUnsafe`, whose own doc comment says "Unsafe for concurrent use" — it does a bare `a.conf.GlobalTags = tags` write, while `pkg/trace/agent/agent.go` (hot path, lines 531/711) and `pkg/trace/api/telemetry.go` read `a.conf.GlobalTags` with no synchronization at all. `GlobalTags` is computed once at config-build time, before the trace agent starts running, and every one of those readers assumes that invariant holds forever — MicroVM's dynamic per-invocation tag update is the only thing in the codebase that breaks it. In practice the write is a pointer swap to a new map rather than an in-place mutation, so the realistic worst case is a span in flight at the moment of the swap missing `lambda_microvm_id` — not a crash. But it's a genuine data race under the Go memory model: `go test -race` / `bazel test --config=race` will flag it the moment a concurrent test exercises this path, and nothing guarantees it stays benign under future compiler optimizations. The fix avoids touching any code shared with the non-serverless trace agent (`pkg/trace/agent`, `pkg/trace/api`, `pkg/trace/config`) by reusing `SpanModifier`, which already runs at the identical point in `agent.go`'s span-processing loop (right after the `GlobalTags` loop) and is exclusively serverless-owned. Its `tags` field existed before this change but was dead code — written by `SetTags`, never read by `ModifySpan`; this fix makes it real. This is scoped entirely to MicroVM. Every other cloud service (`AppService`, `CloudRun`, `ContainerApp`, `CloudRunJobs`) ignores `LifecycleCtx` in `Init`, so they never invoke the async closures — they only ever call the original, still-synchronous `SetTags` once at startup, unchanged by this PR. ### Describe how you validated your changes Added regression coverage for every change (7 new/extended tests): - `TestSpanModifierSetTagsConcurrentWithModifySpan` — hammers `SetTags`/`ModifySpan` from two goroutines under the race detector; this is the actual bug repro. - `TestSpanModifierModifySpanBeforeSetTags`, `...AppliesTagsSetDynamically`, `...ReflectsLatestSetTags` — functional coverage of the new atomic-pointer-backed tag application. - `TestServerlessTraceAgentSetTagsUpdatesGlobalTagsAndSpanModifier` — confirms the untouched synchronous `SetTags` path still updates both `GlobalTags` and the span modifier. - `TestServerlessTraceAgentUpdateRuntimeTagsDoesNotTouchGlobalTags` — the core assertion: `UpdateRuntimeTags` never writes `GlobalTags`. - `TestServerlessTraceAgentUpdateRuntimeTagsNoSpanModifier` — no-op safety when `SpanModifier` doesn't implement `taggable`. - Extended `TestSetupWithoutAPIKey` to also exercise `noopTraceAgent.UpdateRuntimeTags`. Run locally with: ```sh dda inv test --targets=./pkg/serverless/trace,./cmd/serverless-init,./cmd/serverless-init/lifecycle,./cmd/serverless-init/cloudservice --race dda inv linter.go --targets=./pkg/serverless/trace,./cmd/serverless-init,./cmd/serverless-init/lifecycle,./cmd/serverless-init/cloudservice ``` All 302 tests pass (4 skipped, platform-gated) with the race detector enabled; linter reports 0 issues. ### Additional Notes Stacked on #53096 (`tianning.li/microvm-07-05-main-wiring`) — base branch will move to `main` once that merges. `BUILD.bazel` files were checked (`bazel run //:gazelle -- update` + buildifier on the one Gazelle-managed directory touched, `cmd/serverless-init/lifecycle`); no changes needed since the rest of the touched files are under pre-existing `gazelle:exclude` directives (not yet Bazel-migrated). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: Prototype: Swinging Door Compression (SDC) streaming compression for check metrics
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Prototypes streaming, bounded-error compression via Swinging Door Trending/Compression (SDC) with an EWMA-smoothed adaptive tolerance, for check metrics, so a check sampled at 1Hz ships full granularity only where the signal actually moves, and collapses to ~1 point per 15s flush window where it's flat. - `pkg/aggregator/internal/sdc`: the core compressor — a single-pass, O(1)-per-sample Swinging Door Trending/Compression implementation with a per-point tolerance (EWMA scale estimate + swing-door segment tracking). Includes a fix for a real correctness gap in the naive swing-door algorithm (a candidate can keep the intersected slope cone non-empty while its own slope already sits outside it, silently misrepresenting an earlier point beyond tolerance) — see the compressor's tests and comments for the concrete counterexample. - `pkg/aggregator/sender/sdcsender`: a `SenderManager`/`Sender` decorator that applies the compressor to `Gauge`/`Count`/`Rate`/`MonotonicCount`/`GaugeWithTimestamp`/`CountWithTimestamp` calls, selected per check name at `loader.Load()` time (`pkg/collector/scheduler.go`). This works for any check loader (Go, Python, ...) since every loader reaches the aggregator exclusively through this same interface — no changes to `CheckSampler` or the aggregator core. `Rate`/`MonotonicCount` replicate their delta/reset-detection logic locally, since the `Sender` interface carries no timestamp for the real aggregator-side state to hook into. - Telemetry (`sdcsender_samples_total` / `sdcsender_breakpoints_total`, tagged by metric name) makes the per-metric compression ratio observable directly. - A dry-run mode (`checks.sdc_compression_dry_run`) runs every sample through the compressor for measurement, but ships the check's original, uncompressed calls — useful for evaluating what compression would do before turning it on for real. ### Motivation Checks currently emit at a fixed interval (typically 15s), which is a fixed trade-off between granularity and volume for every signal shape. This prototype explores sampling faster (1Hz) and letting a bounded-error compressor decide, per metric, how many points are actually needed to reconstruct the signal within tolerance — full resolution for spikes/steps, minimal for flat/smooth signals. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `pkg/aggregator/internal/sdc`: unit tests assert the bounded-error property across synthetic signals (flat, ramp, spikes, step, near-zero jitter, random walk) and a dedicated regression test for the swing-door correctness fix. - `pkg/aggregator/sender/sdcsender`: unit tests cover compression routing per metric kind, spike/flat/window-boundary behavior, Rate derivative computation, MonotonicCount reset detection, tag-order independence, dry-run forwarding, and pass-through of unintercepted `Sender` methods. - End-to-end, live: built a custom agent and ran it against a local Docker Compose testbench (real agent + fakeintake) with a scripted OpenMetrics endpoint serving a flat signal, a step, a spike, and a monotonic counter. Verified via `fakeintake` that: - the flat signal and the monotonic counter (whose per-scrape delta is constant) both compress to ~1 point per 15s window, - the step and spike signals ship extra points exactly at their real transitions, - dry-run mode ships the exact same uncompressed points as with `sdcsender` absent, while `samples_total`/`breakpoints_total` still show the would-be compression ratio (e.g. ~10:1 for the flat signal). ### Additional Notes This is a prototype/experiment, not production-ready: - The check-name allowlist (`checks.sdc_compression_checks`) and compressor parameters (epsilon/alpha/floor) are placeholders pending real-world tuning. - The real (Python) `openmetrics` check itself hasn't been exercised end-to-end in this sandbox (no Python/rtloader support here); the throwaway `vbrscrapeprobe` stand-in check used earlier for that verification has since been removed now that manual verification against a real agent covered the same `Sender` interface path. - Backend/staging interpretation of the resulting irregular-timestamp series (rollups, graphing) hasn't been verified. Renamed from the internal "VBR" (variable bit rate) codename to "SDC" (Swinging Door Compression) throughout, since that's the actual, well-known algorithm this implements.

signals.title: [CWS] Put back subreaper reparenting
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Restores subreaper reparenting support and hardens process cache lineage handling for runtime security. This PR: - Reads live PPid from the kernel process context instead of storing PPid in `pid_cache_t`. - Adds task struct offsets required to read `real_parent->tgid`, including fallback and BTFHub constants. - Removes reverse `Children` links from process cache entries to avoid retaining large stale process subtrees. - Replaces eager child reparenting with lazy direct-edge reparenting from procfs or kernel PPid observations. - Preserves exec chains when reparenting by updating the fork-root edge rather than replacing the current exec head. - Updates PPid only after a successful parent relink. - Adds `StopExecutionTime` so exec replacement time is distinct from final process `ExitTime`. - Marks full same-PID exec chains exited on final exit or PID replacement. - Repairs target process lineage for ptrace tracees and signal/setrlimit targets. - Adds reparenting metrics and callpath tags. - Updates generated model accessors, marshalling/unmarshalling, deep copy handling, docs, and tests. ### Motivation Subreaper reparenting can happen after `do_exit`, which means process lineage observed from eBPF events can temporarily point to an exited parent. The previous approach kept reverse child references in `ProcessCacheEntry`, which made stale lineage expensive and could retain large process trees under high process churn, such as build-cluster workloads. This PR simplifies the cache ownership model by removing reverse child links and repairing lineage lazily when affected processes are observed. It also fixes exec-chain behavior so reparenting does not collapse or corrupt same-PID exec history, and clarifies the difference between an exec replacement and a true process exit. ### Describe how you validated your changes Validation performed: - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/security/resolvers/process` - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/security/probe` - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/security/secl/model` - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/security/seclwin/model` ran with no tests under this configuration. The diff also adds and updates resolver/model tests for subreaper reparenting, lazy repair, exec-chain reparenting, `DequeueExited`, and `StopExecutionTime` behavior.

signals.title: fix(serverless-init): prevent stale log tag cache prime from clobbering /run update
signals.text: ## Summary - Background: `cachedTags` is an `atomic.Pointer[string]` (not a plain `string`, as on `main` before serverless-init supported MicroVM) because MicroVM's `/run` lifecycle hook can call `SetServerlessInitTagCache` from the HTTP lifecycle-hook server goroutine concurrently with `Encode` running on the log-processing goroutine. A plain string would risk a torn read (mismatched pointer/length) under that concurrent access; the atomic pointer keeps the hot path lock-free while making updates race-free. - Restores `CompareAndSwap(nil, &s)` (as `jsonServerlessInitEncoder.primeTagsFromMessage`) for `Encode`'s cold-path cache prime, replacing the plain `Store()` that PR #53030 landed in response to review comment [r3530721641](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53030/discussion_r3530721641). - That comment's reasoning ("all callers compute the same tags anyway") only covers `Encode` racing `Encode`. It doesn't cover `Encode` racing `SetServerlessInitTagCache` — a second writer, driven by the MicroVM `/run` hook, that pushes an authoritative, possibly newer tag set into the same field. With a plain `Store`, a stale cold-path write computed before that update can land after it and silently clobber the correct value, reverting subsequent log tags to the pre-launch set. - Only MicroVM exercises this second writer today (verified: `AppService`/`CloudRun`/`ContainerApp`/`LocalService.Init` discard `*TracingContext`; `CloudRunJobs.Init` never reads `.LifecycleCtx`; only `MicroVM.Init` wires `LogsTagSetter` through to `SetServerlessInitTagCache`), so Cloud Run / Azure Container Apps / local mode are unaffected either way. ## Test plan - [x] Added `TestJSONServerlessInitEncoder_ColdPathPrimeNeverClobbersConcurrentUpdate`, which sequences the race deterministically (no goroutines) and asserts the authoritative value survives. - [x] Verified the new test fails against a plain-`Store()` version of `primeTagsFromMessage` and passes against the CAS version. - [x] `dda inv test --targets=./comp/logs-library/processor/...` (with and without `--race`) — all 43 tests pass. - [x] `dda inv linter.go --targets=./comp/logs-library/processor/...` — 0 issues. - [x] `bazel run //:gazelle -- ./comp/logs-library/processor` — no `BUILD.bazel` changes needed (no new files/deps). - [x] `bazel build`/`bazel test //comp/logs-library/processor:...` — pass. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: [procmgr] Show profile and user in list and describe
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Expose spawn identity in the process manager API and `dd-procmgr` CLI: - `list`: adds `profile` and `user` columns (table + JSON) - `describe`: adds `Profile`, `User`, and `Runtime User` (only when the process is running and lookup succeeds) Proto changes: - `Process`: `profile`, `user` - `ProcessDetail`: `profile`, `user`, `runtime_user` Implementation notes: - `profile` is derived from the process name (`agent` / `privileged`) - `user` is the intended / last-spawn account, stored on `ManagedProcess` and refreshed on spawn - `runtime_user` is resolved from the OS at describe time (Windows token owner / Linux `/proc` + `getpwuid`) - Windows display formatting is centralized in `AccountName` ### Motivation After Windows spawn profiles land, operators need a simple way to see how each managed child is spawned without reading code or registry state. Showing `profile` and `user` in `list`/`describe` makes SCM migration behavior visible (e.g. process-agent as `privileged` / `NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM` vs other children as `agent` / installer user). `runtime_user` in `describe` helps debug cases where the running PID differs from the intended spawn account. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `cargo test --lib --bin dd-procmgr` (procmgr Rust unit tests) - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/procmgr/coat/...` - Updated procmgr CLI e2e tests for `profile` / `user` / `runtime_user` output ### Additional Notes - `user` reflects spawn policy (intended or last used), not a live registry re-read on every query - `runtime_user` is omitted from `list` and from `describe` when PID is unset or lookup fails (debug log only) - No COAT/metrics changes in this PR

This has been resolved so the PR correctly moves to convert-traces being enabled by default for all paths. ## Summary - Flips the trace-agent's `convert-traces` v1.0 payload-conversion path to be **enabled by default**. - Introduces a new opt-out feature flag, `disable-convert-traces`, for teams/customers who need to revert to the legacy code path. - Updates `pkg/trace/api/api_test.go` to reflect the new default (removes the test-only force-enable of `convert-traces`; the "without conversion" test now sets `disable-convert-traces` instead of clearing the whole `Features` map). - Update serverless use cases to also affect v1 paths (e.g. modify span, discard span) The long term plan here is to deprecate and remove the non-V1 paths. This code change adds some duplicated code for the serverless v1 span usage, but the plan is to remove the old path entirely after we have confidence with customers running the conversion logic and no issues found. ## Test plan - [x] `dda inv trace-agent.build` succeeds - [x] `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/trace/api/...` — all 584 tests pass - [x] We have been dogfooding this conversion logic in staging and production across ALL DCs - [x] APM System-tests pass with conversion logic enabled - [ ] **TODO** Manually trigger APM system-tests to validate on all tracers

signals.title: Support labels in Agent telemetry Python bindings
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? - Extend `datadog_agent.emit_agent_telemetry(...)` with an optional `labels` mapping through rtloader. Existing Python calls continue to work unchanged. - Add both AI-7012 counters to the built-in Agent Telemetry `checks` profile: - `checks.max_returned_metrics_reached` - `checks.max_returned_metrics_dropped` - Preserve the bounded `check_name` and `limit_type` tags on both metric families. Companion changes: - Producer: https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24577 - Public telemetry disclosure: https://github.com/DataDog/documentation/pull/38477 - Tracking issue: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/AI-7012 ### Motivation Support emitting labeled telemetry from Python so the max-returned-metrics signals can include producer identity and distinguish an exceeded effective class default from an exceeded operator-customized limit. The occurrence counter measures how often runs are limited; the dropped-volume counter measures limiter-counted contexts discarded beyond the cap. The producer bounds `limit_type` to `default|custom` rather than exposing arbitrary configured values. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Built the Agent and ran combined OpenMetrics v1/v2 smoke tests against companion integrations-core source. - Verified the filtered COAT payload preserves `check_name` and `limit_type` for both allowlisted metric families. - Ran the focused default-profile configuration test. - Ran the pre-push Go tests and lint.

signals.title: [CWS] Go pprof-label span-context reader + legacy TLS removal
signals.text: ### What Swap the CWS legacy proprietary TLS APM-correlation path for a Go pprof-label span-context reader, on top of the thread-context groundwork. - **Remove legacy TLS**: `fill_span_context_legacy`, the `span_tls` map/struct, its eRPC registration, and the ebpfless ptracer span reader. `fill_span_context` is kept as the dispatch stub. - **Add tail-calls after hooks**: fill_span_context is growing and is inlined in almost every hook. Setup tail-calls after as many hooks to avoid this blowup. - **Add Go pprof reader** (`span_go.h`, `go_labels.go`): reads dd-trace-go's goroutine pprof labels by walking TLS → runtime.g → runtime.m → curg → labels, using per-process offsets resolved from the Go binary. Labels are parsed lazily in userspace to both reduce code blowup and processing time in eBPF. - **Misc**: tolerate a missing login UID (ENOENT); drive the procfs resolver test with a spawned child. ### Testing Functional tests `TestGoSpan` and `TestDDTraceGoSpan` pass.

signals.title: refactor(fleet): make procmgr an independent Linux service manager
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes `procmgr` (`dd-procmgrd`) a first-class Linux service manager in the fleet installer, peer to systemd / upstart / sysvinit, instead of a systemd sub-unit that the installer cannot reason about. - New `service.ProcmgrType`, selected when the init system is systemd, `dd-procmgrd` is installed, and the operator has not opted out. New `pkg/fleet/installer/packages/service/procmgr` package whose unit-level verbs delegate to `systemd`, so no `ProcmgrType` branch calls `systemd.*` directly. - `agentService` gains a flat `Procmgr*` field group mirroring the existing `Upstart*`/`Sysvinit*` pairs, and every service-manager `switch` gains a `case service.ProcmgrType:`. `SystemdUnits*` drops `datadog-agent-procmgr.service`, so `systemd` means plain systemd again. - **Two generated unit trees**: `tmpl/gen/{systemd,procmgr}/<flavor>/`, each with its own `Wants=`. This is what makes the managers independent at the artifact level, and it replaces the `ConditionPathExists=!.../processes.d/datadog-agent-ddot.yaml` gate that had a systemd unit inspecting procmgr's state directory. New `embedded.GetProcmgrUnit` / `GetProcmgrConfig`. - The DDOT extension hooks stop touching procmgr configs entirely, and `writeDDOTProcmgrConfig`/`removeDDOTProcmgrConfig` are deleted. Process definitions are shipped unconditionally from `ProcmgrProcesses*`, exactly like units: `condition_path_exists` decides whether the payload runs, the same way `ConditionPathExists=` does for `datadog-agent-security.service`. ### Motivation From the installer's point of view procmgr was invisible: `agentService.SystemdUnitsStable` listed both `datadog-agent-ddot.service` and `datadog-agent-procmgr.service`, `datadog-agent.service` wanted both supervision paths, and mutual exclusion lived in a unit-file condition. The DDOT `processes.d` config was written from `postInstallDatadogAgent` outside the abstraction — and *not* written by `postStartExperiment`/`postPromoteExperiment`, which relied on the extension hook firing indirectly. That combination made classic-systemd/procmgr interactions hard to reason about and left no way to opt out on Linux. ### Describe how you validated your changes New tests, aimed at the invariants this design rests on: - `SystemdUnits*` contains no `-procmgr` unit and `ProcmgrUnits*` no `-ddot` unit; every name in each array resolves in its own generated tree for all four flavors (both write paths hard-fail on a missing embed, so drift would otherwise surface only at install time). - The generated `datadog-agent.service` `Wants=` matches the tree's array — the guarantee that replaced the deleted `ConditionPathExists=!` gate. - `procmgrInstallRoot` matches `DD_PM_CONFIG_DIR` in the generated procmgr units, for every package type and lifecycle half. This spans a Go helper and a generated unit, and nothing enforced it before; verified by injecting drift and confirming the test fails. Manual review of the generated trees: procmgr tree only defines datadog-agent.service with the specific Wants= sub-service that includes procmgr.service and excludes ddot.service. The yaml processes configuration are generated outside the platform scope: does depend on the platform only the package.

signals.title: autodiscovery: check namespace when suppressing config discovery
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54263 added suppression of config discovery when a manual `openmetrics` or `prometheus` check exists, but that check was too broad for host-wide configs because it did not account for metric namespaces. This PR keeps suppression broad only for generic scraper templates matched to the same service, and makes host-wide static generic scraper suppression namespace-root aware. - If a service already has a matched `openmetrics` or `prometheus` template, drop all discovery templates for that service. - If a host-wide static `openmetrics` or `prometheus` config claims a namespace root, drop only discovery templates whose expected namespace root matches it. - Add `discovery.metrics_prefix` support (see https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24861) on `integration.Config` so integrations whose metric namespace differs from their check name can declare the namespace root used for host-wide conflict detection. ### Motivation [DSCVR-640](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/DSCVR-640) ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit and E2E tests [DSCVR-640]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/DSCVR-640?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signals.title: fix(otel-metrics): skip client-computed spans in OTLP stats concentrator
signals.text: ## What Datadog tracing libraries can emit spans as OTLP while also computing APM stats client-side (CSS). Those spans carry `_dd.stats_computed` as a resource or span attribute. Before this PR, the DDOT connector did not inspect that marker. It converted the spans and recomputed hits, errors, and duration, double-counting stats the tracing library had already produced. After this PR, the connector treats `_dd.stats_computed` as a `ResourceSpans`-level signal. When the marker is truthy on the resource or any span it contains, every span in that `ResourceSpans` is excluded from the connector's concentrator. Other resources in the same OTLP batch remain eligible for Agent-computed stats. ## Why resource scope is correct - Client-side stats are enabled or disabled for the whole ddtrace client; there is no partial per-span enablement. - The ddtrace OTLP path emits `_dd.stats_computed` as a resource attribute. - The Agent and built-in collector processors preserve or copy the resource and its attributes when forwarding, batching, splitting, or regrouping trace data. One marked span is therefore sufficient evidence for its containing `ResourceSpans`, but not for other resources that happen to share the same `ptrace.Traces` payload. ## Changes - Detect `_dd.stats_computed` on both resource and span attributes. - Promote a span-level marker to its containing `ResourceSpans`. - Skip every span belonging to a client-computed resource while retaining unmarked resources. - Return before span indexing and top-level detection when the entire payload is client-computed. - Allocate the computed-resource set only when a marker is found. - Treat absent, empty, or `false` markers as not client-computed; other non-empty values enable the skip. ## Performance The same focused benchmark was run at the PR's base commit and current head on an Apple M4 Max with `GOMAXPROCS=1`. The payload contains 10 resources with 10 spans each. | Scenario | Before PR | After PR | Result | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Client stats enabled | ~281.6 us/op | ~0.82 us/op | ~344x faster | | Client stats disabled | ~282.5 us/op | ~283.7 us/op | +0.4%, within benchmark noise | With client stats enabled, memory falls from 114,808 B/op to 712 B/op and allocations from 855 to 5. With client stats disabled, memory and allocations are unchanged at 114,808 B/op and 855 allocations/op. The added no-marker resource scan measures approximately 0.50 us per 100 spans with zero allocations. That is about 0.18% of the baseline conversion cost, or roughly 5 ns per span for this payload. ## Validation ```text bazel test //pkg/trace/otel/stats:stats_test bazel test //comp/otelcol/otlp/components/connector/datadogconnector:datadogconnector_test ``` Both targets pass. Tests cover marker parsing, resource-level markers, promotion of a span marker to its containing resource, and retaining unmarked resources in the same payload.

signals.title: Titouan.guesdon/clusteragent gomemlimit
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Adds support for `runtime.gomemlimit` in vertical scaling recommendations. When the backend recommendation includes a `Gomemlimit` value for a container, the cluster agent now: 1. Parses `RuntimeValues` (keyed by container name) from the autoscaling backend response 2. Includes `RuntimeValues` in the recommendation hash so changes are detected correctly 3. Injects/updates the `GOMEMLIMIT` environment variable on pods via the admission webhook (`pod_patcher`) 4. Forces a pod rollout (instead of in-place resize) when `RuntimeValues` are present, since env vars cannot be updated on running containers via `pods/resize` 5. Persists `RuntimeValues` to the DPA status annotation so HA follower replicas can reconstruct the full recommendation without hitting the backend ### Motivation Go applications expose a `GOMEMLIMIT` env var to cap the Go runtime's memory usage. Vertical scaling recommendations from the backend can now include this value alongside CPU/memory resource requests/limits, allowing the cluster agent to apply it end-to-end. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit tests in `pod_patcher_test.go` cover: - Injection of `GOMEMLIMIT` when not present - Update of `GOMEMLIMIT` when the value changes - Clearing of `ValueFrom` when the env var was previously sourced from a ConfigMap/Secret (Kubernetes rejects env vars with both `Value` and `ValueFrom` set) ### Additional Notes - `RuntimeValues` are included in the `ResourcesHash` so any change to `GOMEMLIMIT` triggers a new recommendation cycle - Constraints filtering (`applyVerticalConstraints`) also prunes `RuntimeValues` for containers that are dropped, keeping hash consistency

signals.title: fix(config): don't let process_config.enabled override explicit settings
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? The deprecated `process_config.enabled` no longer overwrites `process_config.container_collection.enabled` and `process_config.process_collection.enabled` when you set those yourself. It still fills in whichever one you leave unset, so setups that only use the deprecated setting are unaffected. Closes #48048. ### Motivation Setting both of these: ``` DD_PROCESS_CONFIG_ENABLED="false" DD_PROCESS_CONFIG_CONTAINER_COLLECTION_ENABLED="false" ``` resulted in `container_collection.enabled: true`. The deprecated setting is written at `SourceAgentRuntime`, which outranks environment variables, so it silently reversed an explicit request to disable container collection. The only workaround was to drop `DD_PROCESS_CONFIG_ENABLED` entirely. The fix skips the write when the target setting already came from user config: ```go if config.GetSource(key).IsGreaterThan(pkgconfigmodel.SourceInfraMode) { return } ``` The cutoff is `SourceInfraMode` rather than `IsConfigured`, because `IsConfigured` counts infra-mode as user config. `end_user_device` mode sets `process_collection.enabled` at that source, and it is documented as ranking *below* user config. ### Describe how you validated your changes `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/config/setup` passes (334 tests), linter reports 0 issues. New tests cover precedence (4 cases, including the reported repro), a guard that infra-mode does not shadow the deprecated setting, and idempotency. Stashing `process.go` and re-running makes them fail, confirming they exercise the fix. ### Additional Notes The transform now derives `process_config.enabled` from the process collection value it ends up with, rather than from its own input. Consumers OR the deprecated key with the two that replaced it (`comp/core/profiler/impl/profiler.go`, and `IsEnabled` for the Windows `datadog-process-agent` service), so leaving it `"true"` while both replacements are `false` would start the process agent with nothing to collect. Existing values are unchanged: `true` still normalizes to `"true"`, `false` and `disabled` still normalize to `"disabled"`. The cutoff protects config-file values as well as environment variables, which is slightly broader than the issue describes: `process_config.enabled: true` alongside `container_collection.enabled: true` in the same `datadog.yaml` now yields `true` where it previously yielded `false`. That is the intended precedence, but it is a behavior change worth calling out. The old code was not idempotent: the `"false"` branch set `container_collection=true` *and* rewrote `process_config.enabled` to `"disabled"`, so a second pass fell through to the `"disabled"` branch and produced `false` instead. The new tests invoke the transform a controlled number of times rather than relying on `ApplyOverrideFuncs`, which runs an order-dependent number of times in the test suite.

signals.title: [Backport 7.81.x]  Windows: don't let registry DDAGENTUSER_KEEP_RIGHTS fallback override explicit install args
signals.text: Backport 32353f859276f5283be48e7abe1a615891312a63 from #54125. ___ ### What does this PR do? Prevents a `getenv()` fallback (registry-derived `DDAGENTUSER_KEEP_RIGHTS`, service-derived `DDAGENTUSER_NAME`) from silently overriding an explicit value passed via install args on a Fleet Automation install/upgrade. ### Motivation Follow-up to #53958, addressing a [review concern](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54081#discussion_r3642641460) that also applies to `main`. `getenv()`'s fallbacks for `AgentUserKeepRights` (registry) and `AgentUserName` (running service) don't know about raw install args (`ctx.WindowsArgs`), a separate path an operator/Fleet task can use to pass these properties explicitly. Since `msi.Cmd()` always places typed properties after raw args on the final command line regardless of option order, a stale fallback value would win over an explicit one, reversing the operator's intent. `AgentUserPassword` has no such fallback and isn't affected. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `TestArgsHaveProperty`: property present/absent/nil args, no false-positive prefix match, covers both `DDAGENTUSER_KEEP_RIGHTS` and `DDAGENTUSER_NAME`. - New E2E suite `TestAgentKeepRightsFleetUpgrade` (`test/new-e2e/tests/installer/windows/agent_keep_rights_fleet_test.go`), driving the real Fleet Automation experiment lifecycle (`StartExperiment`/`PromoteExperiment`) against a stable baseline pinned to 7.81.0 (the first release with `DDAGENTUSER_KEEP_RIGHTS`), registered in the `new-e2e-installer-windows` CI matrix: - `TestKeepRightsSurvivesFleetUpgrade` — regression test for #53958. - `TestKeepRightsExplicitArgWinsOnFleetUpgrade` — regression test for this PR, using `StartExperimentMSIArgs` to inject an explicit override at experiment time. Both E2E tests passed CI after two fixes to the tests themselves (a log-filename collision from calling `installPreviousAgentVersion()` twice, and pinning the stable baseline version since the pipeline's default "last stable" pointer predates the `DDAGENTUSER_KEEP_RIGHTS` feature) — the underlying fix required no changes. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: apm: use url.template for OTLP HTTP client resource names
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Uses the OpenTelemetry `url.template` attribute when generating resource names for HTTP client spans. Client spans now use `METHOD url.template` when available and retain the method-only fallback otherwise. Server spans continue to use `METHOD http.route`. Both the current and legacy OTLP resource-name paths are covered to keep behavior consistent when operation/resource name V2 is disabled. Fixes #31570. ## Motivation HTTP client resource names currently collapse to the HTTP method even when OpenTelemetry instrumentation provides a low-cardinality URL template. Using the template produces more useful resource grouping without falling back to high-cardinality raw URLs. ## Testing Added focused unit coverage for client URL templates, method-only fallback, and client/server attribute precedence. Local `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/trace/api,./pkg/trace/otel/traceutil` could not run because Windows Defender quarantined the standalone `dda.exe` after its PyPI bootstrap failed with a TLS handshake error. CI is expected to run the required test targets. ## Additional Notes The current commit is unsigned because no local signing key is configured; it will need to be replaced with a signed commit before merge.

signals.title: [WP] Read OTel thread local context records (OTEP 4947)
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds support for reading span/trace IDs from native applications using the OpenTelemetry Thread Local Context Record format (OTel spec #4947) in the CWS eBPF security module. The implementation adds a new eBPF read path that: Discovers the OTel TLSDESC TLS variable offset (registered by user-space) Dereferences the TLS pointer to locate the OTel Thread Local Context Record This targets native applications using ELF TLSDESC (C, C++, Rust, Java/JNI, .NET/FFI, Python native extensions). ### Motivation The OpenTelemetry specification defines a standard mechanism for SDKs to publish thread-level trace context (trace ID, span ID) through ELF Thread Local Storage so that out-of-process readers like eBPF probes can correlate security events with distributed traces. Supporting this standard allows CWS to automatically pick up span context from any OTel-instrumented native application without requiring Datadog-specific instrumentation. ### Describe how you validated your changes * All modified Go packages (probe/erpc, probe/constantfetch, ebpf/probes, ptracer, probe) build cleanly * The C syscall tester compiles successfully with the new otel-span-open command * Added a functional test (TestOTelSpan) that: * Creates a __thread TLS variable in C, computes its offset from fsbase via arch_prctl(ARCH_GET_FS) * Registers the offset with eBPF via the new REGISTER_OTEL_TLS_OP eRPC operation * Fills an OTel Thread Local Context Record with a known trace ID and span ID in W3C byte order * Triggers an open() syscall and verifies the correct trace/span IDs appear in the captured security event ### Additional Notes

signals.title: [ACTP] package and activate par-control
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Packages and activates split-mode PAR on Linux and Windows hosts: - installs `par-control` and process-manager definitions for it and the on-demand executor; - adds Agent package, installer, and Windows executable-resource wiring; - preserves a standard Unix service `PATH` for process-manager children; - adds fake-OPMS support plus Linux and Windows lifecycle/bootstrap E2E suites and CI jobs. Two details about how the definitions delegate to `dd-procmgrd`: - Windows has no console for a service to inherit, so the `par-control` definition redirects `stdout`/`stderr` to `<ETC_ROOT>/logs/par-control.log` instead of the binary managing its own log file. `dd-procmgrd` now creates a missing stdio parent directory rather than silently falling back to inherit on a fresh install. - The PAR definitions set `DD_FLEET_POLICIES_DIR=${DD_CONF_DIR}/managed/datadog-agent/stable`, which `dd-procmgrd` expands from the supervising unit, so a stable or experiment unit selects the matching config tree. Hardcoding the rendered stable path would have made the control plane and executor read stable policies during an experiment while the core Agent read the experiment's. This matches what the DDOT definition already does. Windows keeps reading `fleet_policies_dir` from the registry, as `pkg/config/setup/config_windows.go` does, because there are no experiment services there. Docker and Kubernetes deployments remain monolithic. ### Validation - `dda env dev run -- bazel test //pkg/fleet/installer/packages:packages_test //pkg/fleet/installer/packages/embedded:tmpl_test //pkg/procmgr/rust:dd-procmgrd_test` - `dda inv linter.go --module=test/new-e2e --targets=./tests/privateactionrunner` The installer test now pins the full `DD_FLEET_POLICIES_DIR` value for both definitions; asserting only the key name would not catch a regression to a hardcoded path. Live Linux and Windows E2E execution is left to CI. _Stack 9 of 9; based on #54594._

signals.title: [ACTP] add par-control executor channel
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds the authenticated local gRPC channel between `par-control` and the Go executor: - health and readiness checks; - workflow signing-key synchronization that keeps the executor alive while synchronization is in progress without counting it as an active action. The executor's idle tracking gains a distinct activity counter for this, so non-action work suppresses idle exit while `ActiveActions` still reports only running actions; - action dispatch and terminal outcomes; - Unix-socket and Windows named-pipe transports using the Agent IPC certificate; - message limits sized for large action payloads. This layer introduces the crate's generated-bindings module and the local transport helpers, since it is the first one that needs executor protos and mTLS. OPMS polling and orchestration remain in later layers. ### Validation Focused Go and Rust tests cover the protocol, key synchronization and idle interaction, transport, and message limits. Proto changes are Bazel-validated because Cargo and Bazel use separate generated bindings. - `dda env dev run -- bazel test //pkg/privateactionrunner/par-control:par-control_test //pkg/privateactionrunner/executor:executor_test` - `dda env dev run -- env -u PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR cargo test -p par-control` _Stack 5 of 9; based on #54590 and followed by #54592._

signals.title: [ACTP] add par-control OPMS client
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds the authenticated OPMS client for `par-control`: - ES256 runner JWT signing; - task dequeue, heartbeat, and terminal publication; - runner health checks; - proxy, TLS, retry, and wire behavior matching the Go runner. Orchestration policy remains in the next layer. ### Validation Rust unit and HTTP/TLS contract tests cover request signing, payloads, pacing, proxying, and TLS behavior. Native TLS coverage runs on Linux and Windows. _Stack 6 of 9; based on #54591 and followed by #54593._
signals.author: embeaken

signals.title: [ACTP] orchestrate par-control tasks
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds the production `par-control` orchestration loop. It dequeues tasks with bounded concurrency, starts the executor on demand, synchronizes signing keys, dispatches actions, and publishes outcomes. Executor idle shutdown is self-owned by the Go executor rather than driven by `par-control` process-manager calls. Task heartbeats run from dequeue through cold start, execution, and terminal publication. Runner health checks are independent of task flow, and shutdown drains in-flight work without calling `dd-procmgrd` from the shutdown path. ### Validation - `dda env dev run -- bazel test //pkg/privateactionrunner/par-control:par-control_test` - `dda env dev run -- env -u PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR cargo clippy --manifest-path pkg/privateactionrunner/par-control/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings` _Stack 7 of 9; based on #54592 and followed by #54594._

signals.title: [ACTP] wire split runner ownership
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes the monolithic Go runner stand down when split mode is enabled on supported Linux and Windows host installations. Containers and unsupported platforms keep the monolithic runner because they do not yet launch the complete replacement topology. This preserves the invariant that exactly one runner polls OPMS without disabling the only available runner. ### Validation - `bazel test //comp/privateactionrunner/impl:impl_test` Tests cover Linux and Windows hosts, containers, and unsupported platforms. _Stack 8 of 9; based on #54593 and followed by #54529._
