signals.title: feat(dogstatsd): detect client payload drops
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Detects sustained DogStatsD client-reported payload-byte drops for UDS and UDS-stream clients using telemetry from the normal final aggregation path. When the drop rate exceeds 1%, the Agent reports a per-Agent Agent Health issue containing queue, writer, and unclassified drop totals. The issue resolves after sustained healthy telemetry. This adds two confirmation-period settings: - `dogstatsd_client_drop_detection.unhealthy_confirmation_window` defaults to `1m` and prevents transient drops from opening an issue. - `dogstatsd_client_drop_detection.recovery_confirmation_window` defaults to `30m` and prevents intermittent drops from repeatedly resolving and reopening the issue. ### Motivation This builds on #54381, which exposes DogStatsD client byte telemetry through Agent Telemetry/COAT. Detecting sustained drops in the Agent provides consistent behavior across supported clients and surfaces an actionable Agent Health issue without requiring new client payloads or library changes. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Unit tests covering detection, confirmation, recovery, missing telemetry, restart reconciliation, and multi-worker flush ordering - Fakeintake integration test covering ACTIVE and RESOLVED Agent Health reports - Updated the benchmarks ### Additional Notes

signals.title: feat(ndm): add the workloadbalancing component
signals.text: ## What New `comp/workloadbalancing` component. Subscribes to the shared `HA_AGENT` Remote Config product for per-device workload balancing assignments, distinguished from HA Agent's own documents by an explicit `type` field. - **Registration is unconditional**: it always listens on `HA_AGENT` and reports apply status for its own documents, independent of the local `agent_workload_balancing.enabled` flag. That flag only gates `IsGroupActive`'s effect — nothing calls it yet, that's a following PR. - **Fallback owner**: when `comp/haagent` is disabled on an agent, `comp/workloadbalancing` reports status for anything that doesn't match its own discriminator too, so a document is never silently dropped by both sides. - **Malformed-but-present documents**: reported as an apply-status error *and* keep the group's previous assignment rather than clearing it, since "malformed" isn't the same as "removed." - Wired only into the three binaries that actually run the check-execution worker pool `IsGroupActive` will gate: `cmd/agent/subcommands/run`, `cmd/cluster-agent/subcommands/start`, and `cmd/cluster-agent-cloudfoundry/subcommands/run`. Not `diagnose`, `flare`, `jmx`, `snmp`, `check`, `dogstatsd`, `serverless-init`, or `systray`: none of those run checks through that worker pool, so there's nothing for the component to do there. ## Not in scope here - Nothing reads `IsGroupActive` yet — no effect on check execution until the worker-gating PR. - SNMP's instance-level config field, metric emission, and inventory metadata are separate, following PRs. - The RC schema itself lives in `dd-source`, coordinated separately. ## Testing Unit tests cover: valid assignment (active/standby), malformed-but-present (error + keeps prior state), fallback-owner both ways (HA Agent enabled/disabled), the local flag being off (document still claimed and reported, `IsGroupActive` still `true`), a group's assignment clearing once its document stops appearing in a later poll, and the RC listener always registering regardless of the local flag. > **Note:** This PR was created by Claude

signals.title: [BARX-2009] Drop Agent 6 RC tags on Go modules
signals.text: ## Motivation - Agent releases create a nested Go module tag for every release candidate. These tags significantly increase the repository's tag count and add pressure to GitHub and GitLab. Agent 7 already drops creating these RC module tags; this PR applies the same behavior to Agent 6. See the [RFC](https://docs.google.com/document/d/15XFZ4AKy8Yhyruo7zilTR84j5kV1dI5eFBhoEFfGzhI/edit?tab=t.0) for more info. ## Important Note - Agent 6 RC module dependencies use versions backed by RC tags. After removing those tags, the dependencies must use another resolvable version. We use pseudo-versions derived from the release branch commit, ensuring modules in the same RC can consume each other’s changes without creating nested RC tags. ## Changes - Skip nested Go module tag creation for Agent 6 release candidates. - Resolve Agent 6 RC internal module dependencies to canonical pseudo-versions at the current release branch commit. - Cache each resolved pseudo-version while updating module requirements. - Keep final Agent 6 release tags - Document the Agent 6 RC pseudo-version workflow. - Add unit coverage for tag suppression and pseudo-version dependency updates. ## Tests - `dda inv invoke-unit-tests.run --tests=release` (46 tests passed) - `GITLAB_CI=true dda inv linter.python` - `git diff --check`

signals.title: [NETPATH-873] netpath RC feature fix: include config name in netpath payloads
signals.text: This is a fix for original Network Path via RC introduced in 7.83 Backport motivation: product goal is to release Network Path via RC with 7.73 ### What does this PR do? - Reads `test_config_name` from scheduled and dynamic `NETWORK_PATH` Remote Configuration documents. - Propagates the name alongside `test_config_id` through scheduled checks and dynamic path attribution. - Adds `test_config_name` to Network Path intake payloads when a name is available and verifies it in unit and E2E coverage. - Continues accepting legacy RC documents that do not contain a config name. ### Motivation Network Path configuration names are currently unavailable to the Agent, so emitted traceroute results can identify a configuration only by ID. The corresponding [dd-source change](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/57975) adds the user-facing name to Agent RC content as `test_config_name`. Propagating that value into NetPath payloads lets the backend associate each result with the configuration name while preserving compatibility with configurations created before the rollout. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `bazel test //comp/core/autodiscovery/providers/networkpath:networkpath_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl:impl_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/common:common_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/connfilter:connfilter_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/pathteststore:pathteststore_test //comp/syntheticstestscheduler/impl:impl_test //pkg/collector/corechecks/networkpath:networkpath_test //pkg/networkpath/payload:payload_test` - `bazel build //test/new-e2e/tests/netpath/dynamic-tests:dynamic-tests_test //test/new-e2e/tests/netpath/network-path-integration:network-path-integration_test` ### Additional Notes The Agent intentionally treats `test_config_name` as optional during ingestion so existing stored RC documents remain valid during rollout. Empty names are omitted from emitted payloads, preserving the existing payload shape for legacy and unmanaged producers.

signals.title: [WINA-3031] Upgrade datadog-go to v5.9.1
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? - Upgrades `github.com/DataDog/datadog-go/v5` from `v5.9.0` to `v5.9.1` across the Go workspace. ### Motivation [#incident-59243](https://dd.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C0BQAB1T274) https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3031 `datadog-go v5.9.1` fixes a nil pointer dereference in the Windows named-pipe writer (DataDog/datadog-go#397). The pipe connection is established on first write, so closing a client that never successfully wrote dereferenced a nil `net.Conn` and terminated the process. The Agent Data Plane pre-flight probe triggers this on Windows. It dials the pipe once to prove readiness, then the statsd client dials again on its first write; when that second dial loses a startup race, the deferred `client.Close()` crashed the Agent service with `0xc0000005`. This is intermittent by nature — it needs the first dial to succeed and the second to fail. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `go list -m github.com/DataDog/datadog-go/v5` resolves to `v5.9.1`. - `go mod verify` — all modules verified. - `GOOS=windows go build ./comp/dataplane/...` passes. The fix is in a `//go:build windows` file, so a native build would not exercise it. - Confirmed every changed `go.mod`/`go.sum` line is datadog-go and nothing else. ### Additional Notes Renovate normally owns this bump (it did v5.9.0 in #53234), but `minimumReleaseAge: 7 days` means it would not open a PR until ~2026-08-24. Landing it manually since the crash blocks 7.84. The diff matches Renovate's output file-for-file, so it will simply see the dependency as current.

signals.title: NCM - Execute setup commands in a separate exec channel
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? This is a follow up of https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53927. Initially the issue was that for Cisco ASA devices we needed setup commands to get the full output of certain devices. However Cisco ASA is picky and will not let you execute multiple commands in one exec session. The fix is to execute the commands in a separate exec channel that way we can get the full output. ### Motivation Cisco ASA sometimes has issues when running multiple commands in one exec session. Customer has reported that this is causing an issue with collecting configs for their devices. ### Describe how you validated your changes ### Additional Notes A release note be may needed for this. It depends on if it will also be added to version 7.83.0 that the previous PR is estimated for.

signals.title: feat(workloadmeta): k8s 1.34+ collect DRA ResourceClaim and ResourceSlice in the DCA (off by default)
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Collect Kubernetes Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) objects into the Cluster Agent's workloadmeta store: `KubernetesResourceClaim` and `KubernetesResourceSlice` entities, via kubeapiserver collectors gated on `cluster_agent.dra_collection.enabled`. This is the first of three PRs for DRA accelerator observability. ## What it includes - `KubernetesResourceClaim` / `KubernetesResourceSlice` workloadmeta entities - kubeapiserver collectors (informer-based, parse v1 and v1beta1 shapes) - `ListKubernetesResourceClaims` / `ListKubernetesResourceSlices` store accessors - `dump()` rendering so the entities appear in `workload-list` - tagger prefix registration (a new Kind without a registered prefix panics `BuildTaggerEntityID` on the first collected entity) - `resource.k8s.io` get/list/watch RBAC in the reference manifests - `cluster_agent.dra_collection.enabled` config (default off) ## How to validate unit test cluster-agent workload-list ``` === Entity kubernetes_node sources(merged):[kubeapiserver] id: ip-192-168-49-247.ec2.internal === ----------- Entity ID ----------- Kind: kubernetes_node ID: ip-192-168-49-247.ec2.internal ----------- Entity Meta ----------- Name: ip-192-168-49-247.ec2.internal Namespace: === === Entity kubernetes_resource_claim sources(merged):[kubeapiserver] id: default/real-gpu-consumer-gpu-f7hjs === ----------- Entity ID ----------- Kind: kubernetes_resource_claim ID: default/real-gpu-consumer-gpu-f7hjs ----------- Entity Meta ----------- Name: real-gpu-consumer-gpu-f7hjs Namespace: default ----------- Resource Claim ----------- State: reserved Node: ip-192-168-49-247.ec2.internal Owner Pod: real-gpu-consumer Reserved For Pods: [real-gpu-consumer] Device Count: 1 Device: gpu-0 (driver=gpu.nvidia.com pool=ip-192-168-49-247.ec2.internal request=gpu) === === Entity kubernetes_resource_slice sources(merged):[kubeapiserver] id: ip-192-168-49-247.ec2.internal-gpu.nvidia.com-nnmmw === ----------- Entity ID ----------- Kind: kubernetes_resource_slice ID: ip-192-168-49-247.ec2.internal-gpu.nvidia.com-nnmmw ----------- Entity Meta ----------- Name: ip-192-168-49-247.ec2.internal-gpu.nvidia.com-nnmmw Namespace: ----------- Resource Slice ----------- Node: ip-192-168-49-247.ec2.internal Driver: gpu.nvidia.com Pool: ip-192-168-49-247.ec2.internal Device Count: 1 === ```

signals.title: feat(vdi): add Amazon DCV core metrics
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? - Registers an opt-in Windows VDI core check for Amazon WorkSpaces. - Collects Amazon DCV performance counters through PDH. - Emits DCV metrics, platform tags, and the `vdi.dcv.health` service check. - Treats version-specific optional counters as debug-level omissions. ### Motivation This is the first functional slice of VDI monitoring. It provides useful Amazon DCV performance metrics without depending on privileged session inventory or system-probe, so it can be reviewed and validated independently before adding enrichment. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/collector/corechecks/vdi,./pkg/util/pdhutil` - `env GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 dda inv linter.go --targets=./pkg/collector/corechecks/vdi,./pkg/util/pdhutil` The focused core-check test passed after rebasing onto the latest `main`. `pkg/util/pdhutil` is Windows-only and therefore has no test package on the local macOS host; it was covered by the Windows-targeted lint/compile gate. Manually validated the successful Windows path on an Amazon WorkSpaces Personal host using the non-FIPS Windows artifact from pipeline `131649377` / job `1961998574`: - Installed the artifact built from commit `efc81c6b` and confirmed the Agent reported that commit. - Confirmed the package ships only `conf.yaml.example`; the VDI check was not enabled automatically. - Enabled a minimal `aws_workspaces` / `personal` instance and ran `agent check vdi` successfully. - Collected 151 samples per run across server, session, connection, channel, imaging, and process metrics. - Confirmed `vdi.dcv.health` reported OK. - Confirmed representative monotonic counters such as `vdi.dcv.server.total_sessions` and `vdi.dcv.server.received_bytes` were emitted as counts in rate mode. - Confirmed the expected `vdi_provider:aws_workspaces`, `vdi_protocol:dcv`, and `workspaces_product:personal` tags were present. - Confirmed an instance-level custom QA tag appeared exactly once on metrics and the service check. - Confirmed the long-running Agent scheduled the check successfully with 151 samples and one service check per run, without VDI warnings or errors. ### Additional Notes This PR is the first draft in a three-PR stack. The PRs will be reviewed and validated in order: 1. **[#55009 — Amazon DCV core metrics](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55009)** (this PR) 2. [#55010 — Privileged session enrichment through system-probe](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55010) 3. [#55011 — Windows E2E coverage and CI wiring](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55011)

signals.title: Add agent-data-plane as a code owner of the tagger entity ID prefixes
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds `@DataDog/agent-data-plane` alongside `@DataDog/container-platform` as a code owner of `comp/core/tagger/types/entity_id.go`, the file that declares the tagger's entity ID prefixes. ### Motivation The Agent Data Plane consumes the remote tagger stream and keeps its own mapping from entity ID prefix to its internal entity type. When a prefix is added here, ADP has to make a decision about it — consume it, or explicitly record that it doesn't need to — and today it finds out only after the fact. We'd like to be aware when new entity prefixes are added since ADP will need to either handle or ignore them. A recent example is that `queue_workload` was added, but ADP didn't handle it and so logged warnings about unknown entity prefixes. ### Describe how you validated your changes CI ### Additional Notes For context on the ADP-side change this pairs with: https://github.com/DataDog/saluki/pull/2353

signals.title: Reject unresolved secret handles on the NPM direct-send path
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds `endpoint.CheckAPIKeysResolved` and calls it from `sender.New` (`pkg/network/sender/sender_linux.go`), so that when `network_config.direct_send` is enabled and `api_key` is still an unresolved `ENC[...]` secret handle, the NPM direct sender refuses to start and says why: ``` error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ("ENC[...]"): this process does not resolve secret-backend handles, provide the api_key as a plain value or enable config sync from the core agent (agent_ipc.config_refresh_interval) ``` The check also covers `process_config.additional_endpoints`, since those keys come from the same config and are equally likely to be secret-backed. ### Motivation NTWK-817. A customer set `api_key` via the secret backend (`ENC[k8s_secret@...]`) and enabled `network_config.direct_send`. CNM data never arrived, and nothing in the logs pointed at the cause. What was happening: system-probe wires the **no-op** secrets component (`secretsnoopfx.Module()` in `cmd/system-probe/subcommands/run/command.go`), so it cannot resolve secret handles itself. It only ever receives resolved values from the core agent over config sync (`comp/core/configsync`)— both `agent_ipc.config_refresh_interval` and `agent_ipc.port` default to `0` (`pkg/config/setup/all_settings.go`). With config sync off, `config.GetString("api_key")` returned the literal string `ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, and the direct sender passed it straight through as the `Dd-Api-Key` header. Every payload was rejected by the intake, and because the direct sender has no API-key validation (`DisableAPIKeyChecking = true`) there was no error identifying the key as the problem. Silent data loss. This does not make the customer's setup work — it makes the failure legible. The configuration they still need is in the section below. ### Scope of the check, and why it is not in `GetAPIEndpoints` The check is deliberately **not** inside `GetAPIEndpoints`, even though that is where the API key is read. `module.FactoryDependencies` (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/common.go`) declares `ConnectionsForwarder connectionsforwarder.Component` as a **non-optional** field, and `startSystemProbe` takes that struct — so Fx constructs `connectionsforwarder` on **every** system-probe start regardless of `direct_send`, and its constructor calls `GetAPIEndpoints` and propagates the error (`comp/forwarder/connectionsforwarder/impl/connectionsforwarder.go`). Putting the check there made any system-probe with a secret-backed `api_key` fail to boot outright, taking CWS, USM, and discovery with it — a regression for a large existing population, since that construction was previously a harmless no-op (a forwarder built with an unusable key that nothing read). Keeping the check at the `sender.New` call site means the failure is confined to what is actually broken: the module loader logs the error and skips `network_tracer`, and the rest of system-probe runs normally (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/loader.go`). NPM and USM are both lost, as they share the `network_tracer` module — unavoidable without silently falling back to the process-agent collection path, which would change the deployment topology in response to a config error. Graceful degradation was considered and rejected. `Register()` skips the `/connections` endpoint when `DirectSend` is true, so keeping the module alive without a sender would load eBPF programs, collect connections, and drop them all — the cost of NPM with none of the data, and quietly. ### Customer-facing configuration required for `direct_send` + secrets To make secret-backed `api_key` actually work with `direct_send`, config sync must be enabled so the core agent supplies the resolved value. In `datadog.yaml` (read by both the core agent and system-probe), either TCP: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 # seconds; must be > 0 port: 5008 # any free port ``` or, preferably in Kubernetes, over a socket: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 use_socket: true socket_path: /var/run/datadog/agent_ipc.socket # on a volume both containers mount ``` One of the two transports must be set. `comp/core/configsync/impl/module.go` logs `configsync disabled: ...` and does nothing if `config_refresh_interval <= 0`, or if `use_socket` is false and `port <= 0`. Caveats worth flagging to anyone enabling this: - **Startup becomes dependent on core-agent readiness.** system-probe runs config sync with `OnInitSync: true` and a **10-second** deadline (`configSyncTimeout`, retrying every 2s). If the core agent is not yet listening, system-probe fails to start with `failed to sync config at startup, is the core agent listening on '...'`. Where both start together this is a real race. - **`use_socket` needs a shared volume.** The standard Helm chart does not give the two containers a shared writable run directory by default; an explicit `emptyDir` mounted into both is required. - The only alternative is a literal `api_key` in the config system-probe reads, which defeats the point of using a secret backend. This interaction is currently undocumented — `direct_send` has no entry in `pkg/config/example/system-probe_*.yaml.example`, no description in the generated schema, and no coverage under `docs/`. Documentation is intentionally left out of this PR and will be handled separately. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit: added `endpoints_test.go` covering a plain key, a bare handle, a whitespace-padded handle, a handle in an additional endpoint, and an empty key. `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/process/runner/endpoint` passes; `dda inv linter.go` clean on `pkg/process/runner/endpoint` and `pkg/network/sender`. End-to-end, in a Linux container (arm64, kernel 6.8, CO-RE) with `direct_send: true`, `api_key: ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, `process_config.process_dd_url` pointed at a local stub intake, and no config sync configured: | | before this change | with this change | |---|---|---| | system-probe process | runs but direct sender gets payloads rejected | stays up, socket bound | | `network_tracer` | n/a | `error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ...` | | other modules | none | `discovery` and `event_monitor` both started | | requests reaching intake | payloads sent with `Dd-Api-Key: ENC[...]` | 0 | | `ENC[` observed on the wire | yes | 0 | `dda inv system-probe.build` also verified in the Linux container, since `sender_linux.go` is not compiled on macOS. ### Additional Notes The error message names the offending setting path, so it distinguishes `api_key` from `process_config.additional_endpoints`. The handle itself is included in the message; it is a reference, not a secret value.

signals.title: trace/api: forward DD-EVP-ORIGIN and DD-EVP-ORIGIN-VERSION through EVP proxy
signals.text: ## Summary Add `DD-EVP-ORIGIN` and `DD-EVP-ORIGIN-VERSION` to `EvpProxyAllowedHeaders` in `pkg/trace/api/evp_proxy.go` so server SDK metadata (SDK name and version) survives forwarding to Event Platform intake. Previously these headers were stripped by the allowlist, losing caller-supplied origin identity at the Agent even when the SDK sent them. Closes [FFL-3014](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/FFL-3014). ## Why the general allowlist (not flagevaluation-specific) There is a single shared EVP proxy handler: `/evp_proxy/v1/`–`/v4/` all route to the same `evpProxyHandler` → `evpProxyForwarder` → `evpProxyTransport.RoundTrip`, which applies `EvpProxyAllowedHeaders` uniformly. There is no path-specific branching, so flagevaluation (`/evp_proxy/v2/api/v2/flagevaluation`) hits the exact same code path as every other EVP-proxied destination. This change therefore affects **all** EVP proxy traffic, not just the Feature Flags & Experimentation team's. This is intentional and we discuss tradeoffs below. ## Tradeoff considerations **Why we feel the blast radius is low:** - **Purely additive.** Headers are only forwarded *if the caller sends them*. - **Consistent with existing posture.** The allowlist already relays caller-supplied identity headers verbatim (`User-Agent`, `DD-CI-PROVIDER-NAME`). Adding origin/version is the same kind of operation: "relay what the caller sent" - **`DD-EVP-ORIGIN` is a general EVP convention, not an FFL-specific concept.** The agent itself sets it on its own outbound EVP calls (the logs, dyninst, and otel paths set it too). Letting it pass through the proxy is consistent with how the rest of the platform treats the header. - The Agent never invents these values, it only relays what the SDK sent. A rogue/unrelated client that doesn't send them is unaffected. **One thing worth flagging:** If any *other* EVP consumer were relying on these headers being **stripped** at the agent (e.g., to prevent clients from spoofing origin identity upstream), this change would loosen that guarantee. We assessed this as a non-issue: the current allowlist already forwards `User-Agent` and `DD-CI-PROVIDER-NAME` from callers, so "relay caller-supplied identity headers" is already the established posture, and there is no evidence any consumer depends on `DD-EVP-ORIGIN` being dropped. If such a consumer is later identified, the fix would be to gate forwarding on `req.URL.Path` but that additional complexity is not needed today. ## Test strategy - All tests use the existing `sendRequestThroughForwarderWithMockRoundTripper` harness (mock round-tripper captures outbound requests). No new infrastructure. ## Acceptance criteria (from FFL-3014) - [x] Captured outbound requests contain the exact incoming origin and version values. - [x] Existing EVP proxy tests pass. - [x] No request payload is modified (only headers). [FFL-3014]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/FFL-3014?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

Check the [Dependency Dashboard](../issues/33469) for more information. --- ### Release Notes <details> <summary>bazel-contrib/rules_python (rules_python)</summary> ### [`v2.3.1`](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#231---2026-08-14) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/compare/2.3.0...2.3.1) [2.3.1]: https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/releases/tag/2.3.1 {#v2-3-1-fixed} ##### Fixed - Previous refactor that shipped with 2.3 introduced regression for the experimental repository cache users. This restores the previous behavior ([#​3791](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/pull/3791)). {#v2-3-0} ### [`v2.3.0`](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#230---2026-08-07) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/compare/2.2.0...2.3.0) [2.3.0]: https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/releases/tag/2.3.0 {#v2-3-0-changed} ##### Changed - (gazelle) **BREAKING** rules\_python 1.5.0 or higher is now required. The Python extension selects its standard library list on `is_python_3.14`, which earlier versions do not define. {#v2-3-0-fixed} ##### Fixed - Fixed `py_binary_rule_builder()` / `py_test_rule_builder()` (from `python/api/executables.bzl`) failing at analysis time with a visibility error when used to construct a custom rule from an external module. - (compile\_pip\_requirements) Add the explicit `data` attribute and forward it directly to the generated `py_binary`, so files passed via `data` can be referenced from `extra_args` using `$(location ...)`. - (coverage) The warning about a missing bundled `coverage.py` wheel is no longer emitted as we are now falling back to a pure python wheel ([#​3950](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/issues/3950)). - (gazelle) The Python extension now uses the correct standard library module list for `python_version` 3.13 and 3.14; previously both fell back to the 3.11 list, so modules added or removed since then (e.g. `compression.zstd`, `telnetlib`) were misclassified. The fallback list for unrecognized versions is now the newest available one rather than 3.11 ([#​3978](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/pull/3978)). - (pypi) Allow `uv_lock` to be specified in `pip.parse` without requiring `requirements_lock` (or other os-specific requirement file attributes) to be set. - (pypi) Fixed the fixed-point loop that resolves self-referencing extras (`pkg[extra]` entries in a package's own `Requires-Dist`). The loop compared the number of extras discovered in the current round against the number known before it, rather than against the size of the merged set. As a result it could stop before every extra was resolved, silently dropping dependencies only reachable through two or more `pkg[extra]` hops, and for the common case of a package with no self-referencing extras it never converged at all, running all 10000 rounds while evaluating each wheel's generated `BUILD` file ([#​4039](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/pull/4039)). - (pypi) Requirement `--hash=<algo>:<digest>` pins and Simple API `#<algo>=<digest>` URL fragments are now parsed for all hash algorithms instead of silently dropping everything except `sha256`. Non-sha256 pins are matched against the digests advertised by the index and downloads are verified using the corresponding Subresource Integrity value, and the pins are kept in the requirement line when falling back to `pip` ([#​3972](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/issues/3972)). As part of this, `whl_library` repos created by `pip.parse` now always pass the digest via the `integrity` attribute (SRI format) instead of `sha256`, and the lock file facts store digests as `<algo>:<digest>` values (the facts version was bumped, so cached index information is refreshed once). - (pypi) `pip.parse(uv_lock = ...)` no longer exposes uv workspace/root members that resolve to no wheel or sdist (e.g. `source = { virtual = "." }` or editable installs). Previously these source-less packages were added to the hub's `all_requirements` / `all_whl_requirements` with an alias to a subpackage that does not exist, breaking analysis for anything enumerating the full set such as `modules_mapping(wheels = all_whl_requirements)` ([#​3934](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/issues/3934)). - (pypi) correctly parse the `index_url` for each wheel so that the source registry is forwarded to the {obj}`whl_library`. This is so that the `purl` for `package_metadata` can be correctly constructed. - (pypi) fixed the URL normalization function to correctly handle local paths enabling wheel sources files to point to an absolute path. Currently it supports the `file://<absolute_path>` for linux and windows like paths. We also support envsubst for the said paths from now on. {#v2-3-0-added} ##### Added - (bzlmod) Added MODULE.bazel flag aliases for Starlark-defined flags: `build_python_zip`, `incompatible_default_to_explicit_init_py`, `python_path`, and `experimental_python_import_all_repositories`. - (bzlmod) Added the `{obj}`explicit\_init\_py`` tag class to the `{obj}`config`` module extension for configuring implicit `__init__.py` file generation module-wide. ([#​3997](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/pull/3997), [#​2945](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/issues/2945)) - (cc) Added experimental {obj}`py_extension` macro for creating C/C++ Python extension modules ([#​3283](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/issues/3283)). (cc) Added `libc`, `platform_machine`, `platform_tag`, `soabi`, and `sys_platform` attributes and info fields to {obj}`py_cc_toolchain` / {obj}`PyCcToolchainInfo`. - (pip,python) Added `pyproject_toml` attribute to {obj}`pip.default`, {obj}`pip.parse` and {obj}`python.defaults` to read the default Python version from the `requires-python` field of `pyproject.toml`. - (py\_test) Added an opt-in safeguard against `py_test` targets that silently pass without running any tests. Set {obj}`--@rules_python//python/config_settings:validate_test_main=enabled` to fail the build when a test's main module only contains inert top-level statements (definitions, imports, assignments) and never invokes a test runner ([#​3824](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_python/issues/3824)). {#v2-2-0} </details> --- ### Configuration 📅 **Schedule**: (in timezone Europe/Paris) - Branch creation - At 12:00 AM through 04:59 AM and 10:00 PM through 11:59 PM, Monday through Friday (`* 0-4,22-23 * * 1-5`) - Only on Sunday and Saturday (`* * * * 0,6`) - Automerge - At any time (no schedule defined) 🚦 **Automerge**: Disabled by config. signals.title: refactor(autoinstrumentation): derive SSI mode from exact match
signals.text: ## Description Extract of https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54766 (part 1 of 2) to make review easier. SSI side effects (`DD_INSTRUMENTATION_INSTALL_TYPE`, SSI defaults such as `DD_TRACE_ENABLED`, UST env vars) now follow whether a configuration target or remote-config policy **matched the pod**, instead of a namespace-level `IsNamespaceEligible` approximation. Library selection is **unchanged**: annotations still short-circuit target matching (existing GA precedence). When annotations and a match coexist, only SSI mode follows the match; applied-target/policy metadata and target `ddTraceConfigs` are still skipped until part 2. Part 2 (#54766 follow-up) will introduce unified `resolveInjection` (annotation override, env merge, deny blocking annotations). ### RC policies (main motivation) This change primarily fixes incorrect SSI behavior when **remote-config policies** are loaded. `IsNamespaceEligible` treated a namespace as “SSI-eligible” if *any* loaded policy *could* match that namespace — even when the policy’s K8s selectors did not match the pod being mutated. In practice, policies that **matched nothing on the pod** (e.g. host/OS-only rules, namespace-scoped rules with pod label constraints, or policies targeting another namespace) could still apply SSI-only mutations in that namespace. Target/policy matching already abstained (no target-selected libraries, no target `ddTraceConfigs`, no `applied-target` / `applied-policy` from a match), but the following **SSI side effects** were still injected whenever the pod was mutated — most visibly on annotation-driven lib injection: - `DD_INSTRUMENTATION_INSTALL_TYPE=k8s_single_step` (instead of `k8s_lib_injection`) - SSI default tracer env vars: `DD_TRACE_ENABLED=true`, `DD_LOGS_INJECTION=true`, `DD_RUNTIME_METRICS_ENABLED=true`, `DD_TRACE_HEALTH_METRICS_ENABLED=true` - UST env vars from pod metadata: `DD_VERSION`, `DD_ENV`, and `DD_SERVICE` (owner/label inference) - SSI-only paths such as language-detection-driven library selection That was a false positive: the pod was not matched by any target or RC policy, but was treated as Single Step Instrumentation anyway. After this PR, RC and local targets use the same predicate for SSI mode as for injection: **did this policy/target match this pod?** ## Behavior changes | Case | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Annotated pod in a namespace that *could* match a rule, but pod does not match (e.g. NS+pod selector) | SSI (`k8s_single_step`, SSI defaults) — **false positive** | `k8s_lib_injection` | | Annotated pod with no matching target/policy | SSI if namespace eligible — **false positive** | `k8s_lib_injection` | | Pod matching a target/policy (with or without annotations) | SSI | SSI (unchanged) | | Annotation + matching target (short-circuit) | SSI if namespace eligible | SSI mode from match; libs/configs still from annotation (unchanged GA selection) | Before: mode was derived from “does any rule match this **namespace**?” — optimistic and non-deterministic for mixed selectors. After: mode is derived from “does any rule match this **pod**?” — same predicate as injection matching. ## Related Issue Follow-up to #54766 ## Type of Change - [ ] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [x] Breaking change - [x] Refactor / cleanup - [ ] CI / tooling - [ ] Documentation ## Checklist - [x] Documentation updated if needed - [x] Tests added or updated - [x] No unintended breaking changes (scoped to SSI mode; selection unchanged) ## How Has This Been Tested? - [x] `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/clusteragent/admission/mutate/autoinstrumentation,./pkg/clusteragent/admission/mutate/common,./pkg/clusteragent/admission/mutate/appsec` - New `ssi_mode_test.go` covers: - annotation-only outside policy scope → lib-injection - mixed NS+pod RC policy → lib-injection when pod labels wrong, SSI when full match - `enabled_namespaces` GA path still SSI on match - annotation short-circuit preserves GA lib selection while mode follows match - Existing `target_matching_test.go` / `rc_policies_test.go` still exercise `getMatchingTarget` ## Additional Notes - Removes dead selector fields from `targetInternal` (matching already delegated to policy engine). - Removes `IsNamespaceEligible` from `MutationFilter` (only `ShouldMutatePod` was used by callers). - DCA release note: `releasenotes-dca/notes/ssi-mode-from-exact-match-cb29a68ef459e96e.yaml`

signals.title: Add concurrency test for flare archive name uniqueness
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a test that races many goroutines through `getArchiveName()` in `comp/core/flare/helpers/builder.go`, asserting no two calls ever produce the same archive filename. No production code changes: #54911's PID+counter suffix already guarantees this, but it was only covered by a single-threaded, same-timestamp test (`TestGetArchiveNameIsUniqueWithinSameSecond`). This adds a companion test that exercises real concurrent callers instead. ### Motivation We considered reverting #54911 in favor of relying on a higher-precision timestamp alone, but a concurrency test proved that `time.Now()`'s effective resolution is not a reliable uniqueness mechanism on its own — even on Linux, concurrent goroutines can read the identical nanosecond value. #54911's PID+counter suffix is what actually guarantees uniqueness, so we're keeping it as-is and locking in the guarantee with a test that mirrors the real production race: the `/agent/flare` HTTP handler and the remote-config listener independently calling `Save()` around the same time. Jira: FLREM-148, FLREM-150 ### Describe how you validated your changes - `dda inv test --targets=./comp/core/flare/... --no-cache --race`, repeated multiple times, all passing.

signals.title: [AAD-6] Unify detector point windows
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? > [!NOTE] > 1. This is mostly for metrics that arrive every 15s, I'm thinking about how to properly manage logs that are every 1s in a future PR (instead of a 30m retention they have 2m retention this way) -> [comment](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55024#discussion_r3802840340). > 2. The end goal is to unify storage when we do the warmup, some values are duplicated (future PR). This unifies all detectors (except RRCF) with an interface to get the min / max number of points per series. This way there is no discrepancy with the storage max retention (now deduced by default [1]). Warmup lazy behavior: Max retention behavior [2]: Detectors follow these conditions: 1. A new series has < min points -> no detector state created (discarded) 2. A new series has min points -> create initial state 3. The series has > min and < max points -> process + can trigger anomalies 4. The series has < min points now but had before > min points -> process (update state only if needed) but don't trigger anomalies 5. Internal detector states have max MaxPoints state points (we don't have a state for a point not present in the storage) 6. A new series can't have > max points nor > max state points (eviction) It improves memory / CPU since series that have few points don't have state, it's lazy computation. It's a tradeoff but it makes more sense to not save the states of points that are stale. Extra changes: - Bocpd has less points: (120, 200) -> (60, 120) - Added all the min / max points to the config Benchmark (all detectors enabled): Overall metric | Baseline | Changed | Delta -- | -- | -- | -- In-use heap, average | 261.02 MB | 135.29 MB | **-48.16%** Detector-phase time, average | 10.751 s | 9.835 s | **-8.52%** Macro F1 | 0.265206 | 0.267651 | +0.92% Macro precision | 0.332990 | 0.491846 | +47.70% Macro recall | 0.578832 | 0.511810 | -11.58% Predictions | 682 | 420 | -38.42% ### Motivation Memory / cpu optimization + unify detectors ### Describe how you validated your changes ### Additional Notes [1] The max retention time is based on 15s / point -> `15 * max(detectors.MaxPoints) + 16` seconds [2] This is enforced by the retention time deduced by the max points for each detector so storage is always big enough We need to fine tune again to improve the scores (all detectors enabled): Scenario | F1 baseline → changed | Detector phase | Heap -- | -- | -- | -- block-building-outage | 0.285714 → 0.000000 | 22.3 → 9.7 ms | 194.7 → 39.2 MB byzantine-fault-cascade | 0 → 0 | 128.815 → 117.926 s | 1216.5 → 1219.1 MB cascading-regional-outage | 0.063224 → 0.000000 | 9.2 → 5.4 ms | 165.7 → 29.3 MB cassandra-repair-degradation | 0.318046 → 0.641981 | 48.2 → 19.5 ms | 294.8 → 62.6 MB dns-upstream-outage | 0.052606 → 0.025667 | 14.0 → 6.5 ms | 182.9 → 46.3 MB kafka-partition-saturation | 0.117641 → 0.108369 | 32.8 → 20.4 ms | 248.4 → 55.1 MB lock-contention-cascade | 0.971969 → 0.365964 | 8.9 → 3.6 ms | 141.5 → 45.4 MB memcached-eviction-storm | 0.057796 → 0.115670 | 13.5 → 4.2 ms | 129.6 → 26.8 MB pool-exhaustion | 0.093612 → 0.097034 | 9.2 → 5.5 ms | 119.1 → 15.9 MB redis-billing-latency | 0.604642 → 0.928561 | 17.6 → 9.4 ms | 185.9 → 32.6 MB redis-cpu-saturation | 0.615742 → 0.928561 | 13.7 → 5.6 ms | 147.2 → 32.6 MB tiered-cascading-outage | 0.001476 → 0.000000 | 10.1 → 3.7 ms | 106.0 → 18.6 MB

signals.title: Pass the lint build tags to --only-modified-packages discovery
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Passes the build tags `golangci-lint` will use to the package discovery done by `dda inv linter.go --only-modified-packages`. ### Motivation `linter.go` passes no build tags, so `process_input_args` turns them into `[]` and `get_modified_packages` skips its `go list` filter (gated on `if build_tags:` since #54890). A modified package whose files are all excluded by the lint tags is then handed to `golangci-lint` as an explicit target, and the run fails with: ``` level=error msg="[linters_context] typechecking error: build constraints exclude all Go files in .../pkg/security/tests/syscall_tester/go" ``` A `./pkg/...` wildcard skips such packages silently, an explicit package name does not, which is why CI (explicit `--targets`, recursive) is unaffected and only the `go-linter` pre-push hook fails. Callers that intentionally pass no tags, such as the Bazel-driven test task, keep skipping the filter. ### Describe how you validated your changes On a branch that modifies `pkg/security/tests/syscall_tester/go`, whose only file is behind `//go:build syscalltesters`: - before: the hook fails with the error above - after: `All linters passed`, and the target list is identical to the one produced before #54890 ### Additional Notes Only affects `--only-modified-packages`, which CI does not use.

signals.text: Backport f7eb778bcf5c8b68482635889f31f051d20b9140 from #55001. ___ This is a fix for original Network Path via RC introduced in 7.83 Backport motivation: product goal is to release Network Path via RC with 7.73 ### What does this PR do? - Reads `test_config_name` from scheduled and dynamic `NETWORK_PATH` Remote Configuration documents. - Propagates the name alongside `test_config_id` through scheduled checks and dynamic path attribution. - Adds `test_config_name` to Network Path intake payloads when a name is available and verifies it in unit and E2E coverage. - Continues accepting legacy RC documents that do not contain a config name. ### Motivation Network Path configuration names are currently unavailable to the Agent, so emitted traceroute results can identify a configuration only by ID. The corresponding [dd-source change](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/57975) adds the user-facing name to Agent RC content as `test_config_name`. Propagating that value into NetPath payloads lets the backend associate each result with the configuration name while preserving compatibility with configurations created before the rollout. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `bazel test //comp/core/autodiscovery/providers/networkpath:networkpath_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl:impl_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/common:common_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/connfilter:connfilter_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/pathteststore:pathteststore_test //comp/syntheticstestscheduler/impl:impl_test //pkg/collector/corechecks/networkpath:networkpath_test //pkg/networkpath/payload:payload_test` - `bazel build //test/new-e2e/tests/netpath/dynamic-tests:dynamic-tests_test //test/new-e2e/tests/netpath/network-path-integration:network-path-integration_test` ### Additional Notes The Agent intentionally treats `test_config_name` as optional during ingestion so existing stored RC documents remain valid during rollout. Empty names are omitted from emitted payloads, preserving the existing payload shape for legacy and unmanaged producers.

signals.title: CONTINT-5289 - retry reaching kubelet with HTTPS
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? When setting up the kubelet client if we fail to reach it using HTTPS, we try to reach it using HTTP. In this case, when a component requests the global kubelet client, this one is configured with HTTP, try to set it up with HTTPS again. In case of failure to reach it with HTTPS, return the kubelet client set up with HTTP, this is fine we'll retry later. In case of real failure return an error, we don't want to continue, this is ok as anyway if we kept the old client we'll reach some errors at some point too. In case we succeed, we never retry anymore. ### Motivation users getting stuck with an HTTP connection due to transient error at start, now will benefit from HTTPS connection after some retry. ### Describe how you validated your changes unit test with mock kubelet that denies HTTPS at start then allows it and validate the new client using HTTPS afterward. ### Additional Notes

signals.title: [FA] Back up agent configuration files at every agent start
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Implements the plan in `config-backup-plan.md`: every time the core Agent starts, it writes a byte-exact snapshot of the configuration files it actually loaded into a dedicated directory (`<confdir>/config-backups`). This is a **config-provenance and audit record** — a byte-exact history of the configuration each Agent actually started with, including layers the installer does not own (hand edits, mounted `conf.d`, fleet policies, operator-templated files). It is **not** a disaster-recovery backup. ### Storage layout - Content-addressed archives: `<sha256>.tar.gz` + `<sha256>.manifest.json` sidecar (manifest renamed first, so a visible archive always has a manifest). - Append-only occurrence log `starts.jsonl` (one line per start), capped by line count. - `flock`-based rotation with a 2s timeout; never skips the snapshot, only rotation. - Content-addressed naming means an unchanged config writes zero bytes however many times it restarts, and re-seeing a config never re-writes the archive. ### Component - New `comp/core/configbackup` (`def`/`fx`/`impl`), `// team: fleet-automation`, wired into `cmd/agent/subcommands/run` only (never in `comp/core/bundle.go`, so `agent status`/`agent config` never write a snapshot). - The module forces its own construction with `fx.Invoke` (the `configsync` pattern), because the component exposes no public method. - `OnStart` hook, so it runs after every constructor — right for the provenance goal, wrong for crash-forensics (a config that fails inside the config constructor never reaches it; the installer's transactional design already is the pre-experiment backup). ### Settings (schema, public) `config_backup.enabled` (true), `config_backup.max_snapshots` (10), `config_backup.max_starts_logged` (1000), `config_backup.directory` (empty — derived from `ConfigFileUsed()` so `${conf_path}` (which does not follow `-c`) can never send experiment snapshots into the stable dir). ### Installer integration - `copyDirectory` (Linux) now skips `config-backups` (required for promote correctness + removes the nesting hazard). Windows is already safe via the `*.yaml` robocopy mask; a test pins that. - `getConfigFileSpec` refuses any path under `config-backups`, including the `/managed` fallback branch (loophole closed). ### Extra surfaces - Flare provider: ships manifests + `starts.jsonl` only, never the archives (they contain verbatim config copies including secrets). - `agent config backup list`: read-only listing (digest, timestamp, deployment ID, size) joined against `starts.jsonl`. Validates archive content digest against the name, rejects unsafe entry names, caps decompressed bytes/entry count (gzip-bomb bound). ### Security - No component running as root and no installer path ever reads these archives (restore is out of scope and belongs in the installer with its own threat model). - Manifest records real uid/gid/mode per file so a future restore path must confront that it cannot restore root-owned files from a `dd-agent`-written archive. - `0700` dir / `0600` files (nix), SYSTEM+Administrators ACL (Windows), flare ships manifests only. ## Deviations from the plan (flagging for review) 1. **Module structure**: the plan says `def`/`fx`/`impl` each with their own `go.mod`. The component needs `comp/core/sysprobeconfig/def` and `pkg/util/hostname` (both root-module packages) for the CWS policies dir and hostname, which a separate nested module cannot import (cycle). So it is a **root-module component**, exactly like `configstream` (the plan's own sibling reference for the forcing pattern). No `modules.yml` entry. 2. **`is_experiment`**: the plan says "never inferred from the directory path". On Linux the only signal available to the core Agent is the installer's `-exp` dir naming, so this uses `strings.HasSuffix(resolvedSrcDir, "-exp")`; on Windows it is always `false` (the live dir is always the stable one). `deployment_id` comes from `.deployment-id` as the plan requires. 3. **E2E assertion**: the plan's "experiment dir holds the pre-experiment snapshot" relies on `cp -a` copying the history into the experiment dir, which **contradicts** the plan's own "Required, not optional: exclude `config-backups` from `copyDirectory`". I kept the exclusion (per the explicit requirement) and the E2E test asserts the experiment Agent's own snapshot instead. This tension is worth a decision before merge — see the recorded objection in the plan about the out-of-tree store. ## Testing - Unit tests (16) in `comp/core/configbackup/impl`: file selection/exclusions, symlink-not-read-through, external-tree prefix, content-addressed dedup, A/B/A/B flap (2 archives, 4 log lines), rotation never-evict rules, permissions, read-only dir, flock contention, stale tmp cleanup, truncated-archive detection, `ConfigFileUsed()==""` not writing to `.`. - Installer tests: `getConfigFileSpec` refuses `/config-backups/*` and `/managed/config-backups/*`; `copyDirectory` skips `config-backups`; Windows `*.yaml` mask test. - `dda inv agent.build --build-exclude=systemd` passes; smoke-tested the built agent (snapshot + manifest + starts.jsonl written, `agent config backup list` works). - E2E test added to the existing `tests/fleet` config suite (Linux-only). **Not run** — requires AWS infra; CI job already covers `./tests/fleet`. - Lints: `lint-components`, `lint-fxutil-oneshot-test`, `github.lint-codeowner`, `linter.go` on the new-e2e fleet target — all pass. ## Open questions for reviewers 1. The `copyDirectory` exclusion vs. the "pre-experiment snapshot in the experiment dir" goal — which behavior is wanted? (The plan is internally contradictory here.) 2. Should `security-agent.yaml`, `system-probe.yaml`, `application_monitoring.yaml` be excluded or scrubbed from v1 (they are root-owned and not `dd-agent`-writable)? 3. `is_experiment` heuristic — acceptable, or should the out-of-tree store be revisited instead? --- ## Sub-agent review findings (3 parallel reviewers) Three reviewer sub-agents reviewed the diff (component correctness/security, installer lifecycle, tests/CLI/E2E). Findings and dispositions: ### Applied in follow-up commit `7fab22183c` - **HIGH (component)** — `evictSnapshots` never evicted orphaned archives (those whose start records were trimmed or never written), so `max_snapshots` was not a hard bound and orphans inflated `toEvict`. Now candidates are built from every archive on disk. Added a test. - **HIGH (tests)** — E2E `promote-keeps-history` assertion was trivially satisfied by the pre-existing stable snapshot. Now asserts the count strictly grows. - **MEDIUM (component)** — archive temp file was not `fsync`ed before rename; a crash could leave a zero/partial archive under the final name. Added `tmp.Sync()`. - **MEDIUM (installer)** — `copyRegularFile` failed hard on `os.Lchown` EPERM when running as non-root; now logs and continues, matching `cp -a`. - **LOW (component)** — `walkTree` used `d.Type()` which can misreport regular files on filesystems without `d_type`; now uses `info.Mode().IsRegular()`. - **MEDIUM (tests)** — added unit tests for the full `backup()` happy path, `enabled=false`, the `directory` override, and the positive digest-verification path. - **LOW (tests)** — E2E count check moved inside `EventuallyWithT` to avoid a publish race. ### Disputed (reviewer error, verified) - Installer reviewer claimed `delete`/`delete-all` bypass the `config-backups` guard. **Incorrect**: `getConfigFileSpec` is consulted at the top of `FileOperation.apply` for all operation types, so delete is refused too (verified with a test). ### Left as open questions (design decisions, not mechanical fixes) - **HIGH (installer)** — Linux `replaceConfigDirectory` deletes the old stable's `config-backups` on promote (renames stable to a temp dir, then `RemoveAll`s it). With the `copyDirectory` exclusion, the promoted stable therefore holds only the experiment's own snapshots; the pre-experiment history is lost on promote. The plan's "history is continuous" goal needs a decision: preserve/merge the old stable history across promote (e.g. rename it into the new stable's `config-backups`), or accept the loss and rely on the out-of-tree store from the plan's recorded objection. **This is the single most important open question.** - **MEDIUM (installer)** — `copyDirectory` is not a full `cp -a` equivalent (no hard links, timestamps, xattrs/ACLs, setuid/setgid/sticky). Likely fine for a config dir; documenting. - **LOW (component)** — `cleanStaleTmp` can delete a concurrent publish's temp file (runs without the rotation lock); archive-exists check treats any non-IsNotExist error as "exists". - **NIT** — `config_backup` schema section has no `full-agent-only` tag; `backup list` surfaces on `cluster-agent config backup list` (harmless, prints "no backups found").

signals.title: fix(e2e): Avoid secret propagation to copy file paths
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Removes secret propagation from the temporary pathname generated by `CopyInlineFile` while preserving secrecy on the inline file contents. This prevents the pathname from tainting the `CopyFile` triggers array as secret and allows Pulumi to serialize the remote copy resource during previews. ### Motivation Inline Agent configuration includes secret values such as the API key. Because the temporary pathname is produced by an `ApplyT` on that content, Pulumi marks the pathname secret even though it contains no file contents. Passing that secret pathname through the remote copy triggers caused previews to fail with `malformed RPC secret: missing value for "triggers"`. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Ran `dda inv test --module=./test/e2e-framework --targets=./components/command/...`. - Reproduced the preview failure with both Pulumi CLI 3.257.0 and 3.253.0 before the change. - Ran `dda inv aws.create-vm --use-fakeintake` after the change. Pulumi preview completed and the update successfully created all 29 resources, including the EC2 host, healthy fakeintake ECS service, and running Agent.

signals.title: Add PostgreSQL collector for Config Files Discovery
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Adds a PostgreSQL collector to Config Files Discovery (`comp/core/configfilesdiscovery`), modeled on the Redis collector added in #54375. It collects: - `postgresql.conf`, resolved via (in order) an explicit `config_file` argv setting, an explicit `-D` data directory, or a `PGDATA`-derived fallback (`$PGDATA/postgresql.conf`). No default path is hardcoded — without an explicit source or a usable `PGDATA`, no file is collected. - A small allow-listed set of non-secret environment variables: `PGDATA`, `POSTGRES_DB`, `POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD`, `POSTGRES_INITDB_WALDIR`. Everything else — passwords, `PGSSL*`, `DATABASE_URL`, `POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS`, etc. — is excluded by an explicit deny-list on top of the shared secret-name filter. Ambiguous or conflicting config sources (e.g. differing `-D` values across live processes, or an explicit-but-empty `config_file`) block collection rather than guessing. Also: - Registers the collector in `fx.go`. - Regenerates the affected `BUILD.bazel` files via gazelle/buildifier. - Extends the Docker E2E discovery suite with a Postgres fixture (`postgres:16`, pinned by digest via the ECR pull-through cache) and `TestPostgresConfigFilePayloadSentToEventPlatform`, verifying the payload, allowed env vars, and that no password-shaped variable is ever forwarded. ## Motivation Extends Config Files Discovery's existing Redis/Kafka coverage to PostgreSQL. ## Describe how you validated your changes - `dda inv test --targets=./comp/core/configfilesdiscovery/...` — all unit tests pass. - `dda inv linter.go` — clean. - `dda inv agent.build --build-exclude=systemd` — builds successfully. - `bazel build //comp/core/configfilesdiscovery/...` — succeeds. - Opening as a **draft** to let the Docker E2E discovery suite run in CI (the live/local run against provisioned AWS infra was not run locally). ## Possible Drawbacks / Trade-offs - Uses `PAYLOAD_FORMAT_PROPERTIES` since no dedicated PostgreSQL payload format enum exists yet. - Only launch commands that literally exec `postgres` are recognized; custom wrappers that never exec it are unsupported. - Host/systemd PostgreSQL is unsupported (Config Files Discovery has no `RuntimeHost` reader). - `*_FILE` variants (e.g. `POSTGRES_DB_FILE`) and locale/timezone/`POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS` variables are intentionally not allow-listed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: Set GIT_DEPTH: 1000 for bazel jobs that upload junit data via datadog-ci
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? It changes the GIT_DEPTH for bazel jobs that include junit uploads to 1000, in order to avoid errors and extra job duration time from datadog-ci attempting to retrieve more of the history. ### Motivation https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54834 set the default GIT_DEPTH to 1 (shallow clone). That causes errors from datadog-ci junit upload command (like [here](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1960273838/viewer#L5866)), and makes the savings from the shadow clone be undone by the time that command spends attempting to fetch more git history without success. ### Describe how you validated your changes The `coverage` job got faster by ~2 minutes (from 6m to 4m) and the error logs are gone: https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1961189801 ### Additional Notes - This is a mitigation, probably not an appropriate longterm solution. - I also attempted lower numbers of GIT_DEPTH but they hit the same code path. - The error is coming from [here](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-ci/blob/d5284b8f22d3981b9adb104434aa859cf37fd0b3/packages/base/src/commands/git-metadata/gitdb.ts#L193-L200). `MAX_HISTORY.oldestCommits` happens to be 1000, which is one of the reasons I ended up settling on this number. - 1000 is low enough that the git fetching step takes ~40 seconds, while making the job not waste time on the junit upload stage.

signals.title: Add PostgreSQL collector for Config Files Discovery
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Adds a PostgreSQL collector to Config Files Discovery, following the model established by the Redis collector (#54375). It locates `postgresql.conf` from the `postgres` process's argv (`-c config_file=...` or `-D <data-dir>`), falling back to `PGDATA`-derived path only when no explicit argv source is present, and forwards a small allow-listed set of non-secret environment variables (`PGDATA`, `POSTGRES_DB`, `POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD`, `POSTGRES_INITDB_WALDIR`), filtered again through the shared secret-name heuristic. No config file is ever guessed, and no credentials or secret-shaped variables are ever forwarded. ## Motivation Extends Config Files Discovery to PostgreSQL, mirroring the Redis and Kafka collectors already in this component. ## Describe how you validated your changes - Unit tests: `dda inv test --targets=./comp/core/configfilesdiscovery/...` — 302/302 passed, covering argv parsing/precedence, env-var allow/deny/secret-shaped filtering, and collector-outcome cases. - `dda inv linter.go --targets=./comp/core/configfilesdiscovery/...` — clean. - `bazel run //:gazelle -- ./comp/core/configfilesdiscovery/impl/collectors` + `bazel run //bazel/buildifier` — regenerated BUILD.bazel. - `bazel build //comp/core/configfilesdiscovery/...` — clean. - `dda inv agent.build --build-exclude=systemd` — full agent build succeeds. - Added `TestPostgresConfigFilePayloadSentToEventPlatform` Docker E2E test alongside the existing Redis/Kafka ones. Opening as **draft** to let CI run the Docker E2E discovery suite. ## Possible Drawbacks / Trade-offs - Uses `PAYLOAD_FORMAT_PROPERTIES` since no dedicated PostgreSQL payload format enum exists upstream. - Only launch commands that literally exec `postgres` are supported; custom wrappers (e.g. `pg_ctlcluster`) are not. - Host/systemd PostgreSQL is unsupported, since this component has no `RuntimeHost` reader. - `*_FILE` variants (e.g. `POSTGRES_USER_FILE`) and `POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS` are intentionally excluded from the allow-list. ## Additional Notes Rebuilt on current `main` (previous draft PR #55039 was based on a stale branch and picked up unrelated phantom diffs plus a Bazel regression — closed in favor of this clean version).

signals.title: APM: Fix pkg/trace log format-string bugs
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Fix format-string bugs in `pkg/trace` and add `github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pkg/trace/log` to the govet `printf` `funcs` allowlist in `.golangci.yml` so this class of bug is caught by CI going forward. ### Motivation pkg/trace logger has printf style commands but the govet rule didn't know about this so there were a few spots where the printf directives were wrong ### Describe how you validated your changes - `dda inv linter.go --module=pkg/trace` → `0 issues.` / `All linters passed` (after all fixes; before the fixes it reported the 5 originally-known findings plus 2 additional `%s`-with-non-Stringer findings, all now fixed). - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/trace/agent,./pkg/trace/filters` → all tests pass (403 tests, 3 pre-existing skips unrelated to this change). - `git diff origin/main` reviewed line-by-line to confirm the legacy `*pb.Span` code paths (`normalize`, `Truncate`) were left untouched — on `pb.Span`, `Resource`/`Name` are struct fields and the existing `s.Resource`/`s.Name` usages there are correct as-is. - `dda inv linter.go --targets=./cmd/serverless-init,./comp/core/log/impl-trace,./comp/process/gpusubscriber/impl,./pkg/config/remote/uptane,./pkg/privateactionrunner/bundles/helm,./cmd/process-agent/subcommands/status` → `0 issues.` (sanity check that no other consumer of `pkg/trace/log` regressed). - Added a `fixes:` release note via `reno new trace-log-printf-format-fixes`. ### Additional Notes ### Why not `DebugString()` `*idx.InternalSpan` does have a `DebugString()` helper, and it would satisfy the verb — but it dumps every span attribute. Attributes are unbounded in size and can carry request data (URLs, DB statements, custom tags), which makes them unsuitable for a value interpolated into a log line that fires once per malformed span. Both sites therefore log the identifying fields explicitly instead. `DebugString()` remains available for interactive debugging.

signals.title: fix(autodiscovery): reject null/non-object discovery instances
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? `parseDiscoveryResult` (`comp/core/autodiscovery/discoverer/discovery_json.go`) now rejects a discovered config whose `instances` array contains an entry that isn't a JSON object (e.g. `null`, a number, or an array), instead of silently wrapping the raw bytes and passing them downstream. A malformed result is treated the same way the existing "invalid JSON" case already is: the discovery worker logs a warning and requeues/retries the probe. ### Motivation While reviewing [#54837](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54837) (a `7.83.x` backport of #54660), Datadog's automated Codex reviewer [flagged](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54837#discussion_r3796653045) that a discovery result containing `"instances": [null]` would flow unchanged into `resolved.Instances[i].MergeAdditionalTags(...)` in `applyDiscoveredConfigsLocked`. `MergeAdditionalTags` unmarshals YAML `null` into a map pointer, which resets it to a nil map, and the following `rawConfig["tags"] = []string{}` then panics on that nil map — crashing the whole Agent, with no recovery anywhere in that call chain. An examination of `datadog_checks_base`'s discovery pipeline (`utils/discovery/probe.py`) confirmed that a null instance can't actually reach the Agent today from shipped integrations: a candidate is only accepted after the real check runs successfully against it and submits a metric, and `AgentCheck.run()` fails immediately (`self.instance.get(...)`) on a `None` instance, so such a candidate is always rejected before it's returned. This is therefore defense-in-depth hardening rather than a fix for an observed crash. ### Describe how you validated your changes Added cases to the existing table-driven `TestParseDiscoveryResult` in `discovery_json_test.go` covering a `null` instance, a scalar instance, and an array instance, all asserting `parseDiscoveryResult` returns an error. --- 🤖 This PR description and fix were generated with assistance from Claude Code.

signals.title: incident-59224/incident-59369: cap `tests_windows-x64` build parallelism at 4
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Add `--build-cpus` to the `test` task, so `go build` parallelism (`-p`) can be set independently of test parallelism (`-parallel`), and pass `--build-cpus 4` on Windows while keeping `--cpus 8`. Every other caller keeps its current behavior: the parameter defaults to `cpus` when unset. Not covered: `-p` caps concurrent test binaries as well as build actions, so cross-package test concurrency drops from 8 to 4. Go exposes no knob to separate those two, `-parallel 8` only preserves parallelism within a package. ### Motivation `tests_windows-x64` fails while linking, sporadically from 2026-07-30 and frequently since 2026-08-08. Filed as [incident-59224](https://dd.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C0BQ6LTADFG), then again as [#incident-59369](https://dd.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C0BQXGXCQMC) on 2026-08-18 with the same signature in jobs [1960498027](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1960498027), [1960338207](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1960338207), [1960197554](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1960197554), [1959990966](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1959990966) and [1959329311](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1959329311). The process that dies is Go's own linker, not mingw `ld`: all 25 `errno=1455` dumps in job 1951788199 sit in `loadlib` -> `LoadSyms` -> `preloadSyms`. Eight concurrent linkers reach about 17 GB of commit charge, which exhausts the container. Test execution is not the problem: nine concurrent test binaries totalled 893 MB. ### Describe how you validated your changes Reproduced on a Windows VM with a 20 GB commit ceiling, gcc 14.2.0, Go 1.26.5 and GOMEMLIMIT=2560MiB, running: ``` go test -p N -race -cover -covermode=atomic ./cmd/... ``` Link-only reliability, 3 reps unless stated: ``` -p 8 3/3 OOM -p 7 2/3 OOM -p 6 1/3 OOM -p 5 0/8 clean :+1: -p 4 0/8 clean :+1: ``` Build wall clock, one rep each, **no `-w`**: ``` -p 8 296s 1.00x OOM -p 7 352s 1.19x OOM -p 6 319s 1.08x clean -p 5 309s 1.04x clean -p 4 275s 0.93x clean 🚀 -p 3 282s 0.95x clean -p 2 356s 1.20x clean -p 1 550s 1.86x clean ``` The build time is almost flat from `-p 3` to `-p 8`, so 4 costs nothing measurable while leaving 2 steps of margin below the cliff. `-p 6` came back 3/3 not clean in one batch and clean in another, so the cliff moves between runs and 5 sits too close to it. ### Additional Notes Measured on a 20 GB bare host, not the 24 GB container, without the `python` tag and over `./cmd/...` only, so the ordering transfers but the absolute numbers are not CI's. This caps the legacy `go test` path only. The Bazel test path is capped separately by #55044, and the two compose because `test_flavor` completes before `_run_bazel_tests`. **The `-w` of #54903 is inert**: 2/3 OOM with it against 2/3 without, peaks indistinguishable, because it removes `DwarfGenerateDebugSyms` while the OOM is in `loadlib`. => it can be reverted separately.

signals.title: Revert ineffective "drop DWARF from Windows Go test binary links"
signals.text: This reverts commit 078d86b4fa11aeef88c5150bbc4091c93bfde84b (#54903). ### Motivation `-w` was measured inert against the failure it was meant to mitigate. The OOM is in Go's own linker, not mingw `ld`: all 25 `errno=1455` dumps in job [1951788199](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1951788199) sit in `loadlib` -> `LoadSyms` -> `preloadSyms`. `-w` suppresses `DwarfGenerateDebugSyms`, which runs after `loadlib`, and it does not shrink the linker input either, because the compiler emits DWARF into the object files regardless (`-dwarf` defaults to true). ### Describe how you validated your changes Windows VM, 20 GB commit ceiling, `GOMEMLIMIT=2560MiB`, 3 reps each of: ``` go test -p 8 -race -cover -covermode=atomic ./cmd/... ``` ``` without -w 2/3 OOM peaks 16,581-17,299 MB with -w 2/3 OOM peaks 16,768-17,240 MB ``` Per-phase linker heap on Linux, `-ldflags=-benchmark=mem`, `-race`: ``` Loadlib live DwarfGenerateDebugSyms alloc baseline 420.2 MB 412.9 MB -w 420.5 MB 0 ``` `Loadlib` is unchanged to within 0.3 MB, which is why the OOM rate does not move. ### Additional Notes `-w` does cut peak link heap by 19 percent on Linux, 637 MB to 518 MB, and costs no diagnostics because `pclntab` is untouched. That saving is real but sits on the **wrong side of the failing phase**. Capping build concurrency is what addresses the OOM: `-p 5` was 0/8 clean where `-p 8` was 3/3 OOM, hence: - #55054. Measured on a 20 GB bare host over `./cmd/...` without the `python` tag, so the ordering transfers but the absolute numbers are not CI's.

signals.title: Resolve sysprobe-functional test assets relative to the package source dir
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes `TestUSMAutoTaggingSuite` resolve its fixture files against the package's source directory instead of the process working directory. The suite pushed fixtures to the remote Windows host using bare relative paths such as `"usmtest/test_tags.ps1"`. `CopyFile` opens these as ordinary local files, so they resolve against the *process* working directory. That directory is only the package directory by convention — `go test` chdirs there, and the prebuilt-binary launcher sets `command.Dir` explicitly ([`internal/tools/gotest-custom/main.go`](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/blob/main/internal/tools/gotest-custom/main.go#L77)). Neither is a guarantee. When the test process started from the repo root instead, every asset lookup failed: ``` host.go:257: open usmtest/test_tags.ps1: no such file or directory ``` `SetupSuite` already solved this for the `assets` directory by deriving an absolute path from `runtime.Caller(0)`. This promotes that to a `packagePath` helper and applies it at the seven `CopyFile` call sites, which is where the relative strings are consumed — so the ~36 path literals in `apmtags_testdefs_test.go` are unchanged. Also drops the `testspath` field, which was assigned from `os.Getwd()` and never read, and the stale `// test this out` comment above `copyFileToSiteRoot`. ### Motivation https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3035 The failure is deterministic, not flaky. Datadog test data for this suite on `main` splits cleanly on the reported working directory: | `@test.working_directory` | fail | pass | | --- | --- | --- | | `.` (repo root) | 44 | 0 | | `test/new-e2e/tests/sysprobe-functional` | 0 | 248 | 292 executions, no exceptions in either direction. The suite failed **only** when launched from the repo root, and 100% of the time under that condition. It stopped failing because the runner's working directory reverted, not because anything was fixed — the relative paths are still on `main` today. The failure mode is silent-then-total: the next time build tooling moves the test process's CWD, this suite goes from green to 100% red, and because it is marked `is_known_flaky` it will block nothing while doing so. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `dda inv linter.go --module=test/new-e2e --targets=./tests/sysprobe-functional` → `0 issues`, all linters passed. - No behaviour change when the working directory is already correct, which is the case in CI today. **A green e2e run here does not exercise the failure mode** — both launch paths chdir into the package directory, so the old code passes too. - Reproducing the original failure requires launching the prebuilt test binary from the repo root, which is the one context where neither chdir applies: ``` dda inv new-e2e-tests.build-binaries ./test-binaries/tests-sysprobe-functional.test -test.run TestUSMAutoTaggingSuite -test.v ``` On `main` this fails at `host.go:257`; on this branch it proceeds into the assertions. ### Additional Notes `sysprobe_test.go` has the same class of defect via `os.Getwd()` ([L50](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/blob/main/test/new-e2e/tests/sysprobe-functional/sysprobe_test.go#L50), consumed at [L95](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/blob/main/test/new-e2e/tests/sysprobe-functional/sysprobe_test.go#L95)) and would break `TestVMSuite` the same way. Left out of this PR to keep it scoped to WINA-3035 — it is a two-line change now that `packagePath` exists in the package, and worth a follow-up. A unit test that chdirs and asserts the fixtures still resolve would guard this permanently and run in seconds without AWS. Not included here because the package has no unit-test sibling today and adding one means adopting the `e2eunit` build-tag convention described in `test/new-e2e/AGENTS.md`. Happy to add it if reviewers would prefer it in this PR. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: [Backport 7.83.x] [CWS] Fix: handle activity dump endpoint host that already embeds a port
signals.text: Backport of #54774 to `7.83.x`. ### What was broken in 7.83 This is a **bug fix**. CWS activity dump uploads to dual-shipped `additional_endpoints` whose `host` already includes a port (e.g. `cws-intake.datadoghq.com.:443`) fail. `GetEndpointURL` appended the port a second time, producing a malformed `[host:port]:port` authority that failed URL parsing, so every upload to that endpoint failed with an `invalid port` error. In prod, CWS activity dumps were failing to reach the secondary (dual-ship) endpoint. ### Fix The host is now split before joining, so an embedded port is honored instead of duplicated. An explicitly configured port still wins, and bare IPv6 literals are untouched. ### Automated testing Test coverage is included in this backport (`pkg/security/utils/endpoint_test.go`), reproducing the exact prod host and asserting the resulting URL is accepted by `http.NewRequest` — the call that previously failed. Additional cases cover explicit-port precedence and IPv6 with an embedded port. ### Cherry-pick Cherry-picked cleanly (no conflicts) from `d4251bf9b58f48d1c28070dd662a1ef6d001936f`. Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)
