signal.title: fix(ndm): let comp/haagent skip workload-balancing documents on the shared HA_AGENT product
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Prepares `comp/haagent` to safely share the `HA_AGENT` Remote Config product with a new, upcoming `comp/workloadbalancing` component (part of NDM Agent Workload Balancing). Per the [RFC](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/II/pages/7029621750), workload balancing reuses HA Agent's existing `HA_AGENT` RC product rather than registering a new one, carrying a second, independently-owned payload distinguished by an explicit `type: "workload_balancing"` field — the same discriminator pattern ASM and Network Path's `NETWORK_PATH` product already use for more than one payload type on one product (`NETWORK_PATH` also discriminates via a `type` field). Today, `comp/haagent`'s `onHaAgentUpdate` unmarshals every document on this product into `{config_id, active_agent}`. A workload-balancing document has neither field, so it would silently drop the unknown fields, fail the `config_id` mismatch check, and get reported as an HA Agent apply error — even though it isn't HA Agent's document to own. This adds a minimal discriminator-only unmarshal before HA Agent's existing parse logic, mirroring `comp/core/autodiscovery/providers/networkpath`'s `getConfigType` pattern (which does the same kind of split for the shared `NETWORK_PATH` product). A document whose discriminator unmarshal succeeds with `type == "workload_balancing"` is logged and skipped — no apply-status callback — for `comp/workloadbalancing` to claim and report on itself. Everything else (HA Agent's own documents, and genuinely malformed documents) falls through to today's unchanged unmarshal/`config_id`-mismatch/error-reporting logic. Also fixes a real bug two independent reviewers (Codex and Datadog Autotest) caught on this PR: `onHaAgentUpdate`'s reset-to-`Unknown` only fired on a fully empty batch. With `HA_AGENT` shared, a batch can be non-empty but contain zero HA-owned documents (HA Agent's own document removed from RC, only workload-balancing documents remain), and the stale `Active`/`Standby` state was never cleared. Now tracked explicitly: if no document in a non-empty batch reaches HA Agent's own parsing logic, state resets the same as an empty batch. Also documents `HA_AGENT` as a multi-owner Remote Config product where it wasn't before: `ProductHaAgent`'s doc comment (`pkg/remoteconfig/state/products.go`) now notes it's shared with `comp/workloadbalancing`. ## Why a `type` field, not "non-empty group ID" The RFC originally discriminated on a non-empty group-identifying field, but was revised after review to use an explicit `type` field instead — closer to `NETWORK_PATH`'s own discriminator — and to rename the group field itself away from `group`/`group_id`/`GroupID`. The agent already has a dormant `ha_agent.group` config key and RC schema field reserved for a separate, in-flight proposal to make `agent_group` the canonical HA cluster identity on this same product, replacing `config_id`; reusing `group`/`GroupID` here would have collided with that unrelated, already-claimed concept. `comp/haagent`'s discriminator only needs the `type` field to make its skip decision, so this PR doesn't carry the group field at all. ## Behavior change today No document the backend actually sends today can match the discriminator, since `comp/workloadbalancing` doesn't exist yet. The one real edge case: a document that happens to parse as JSON with `type: "workload_balancing"` for reasons unrelated to workload balancing (a stray/malformed document) previously got reported as an HA Agent error; after this PR it's silently skipped instead, with only a debug log to show it happened. Covered by a release note rather than `changelog/no-changelog`, since this is a real (if narrow) behavior change. ## First in a stack This is PR 1 of the NDM Agent Workload Balancing implementation (`comp/workloadbalancing` skeleton, check-execution gating, metric emission, metadata, and e2e tests follow in separate PRs). This one is standalone and reviewable independently by HA Agent's owning team — it needs to merge and reach the field before workload-balancing RC traffic can safely flow in production. That ordering is a rollout/communication requirement to whoever owns the RC schema and backend writer, not something this PR can enforce in code. > **Note:** This PR was created by Claude

signal.title: refactor(autoinstrumentation): derive SSI mode from exact match
signal.text: ## Description Extract of https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54766 (part 1 of 2) to make review easier. SSI side effects (`DD_INSTRUMENTATION_INSTALL_TYPE`, SSI defaults such as `DD_TRACE_ENABLED`, UST env vars) now follow whether a configuration target or remote-config policy **matched the pod**, instead of a namespace-level `IsNamespaceEligible` approximation. Library selection is **unchanged**: annotations still short-circuit target matching (existing GA precedence). When annotations and a match coexist, only SSI mode follows the match; applied-target/policy metadata and target `ddTraceConfigs` are still skipped until part 2. Part 2 (#54766 follow-up) will introduce unified `resolveInjection` (annotation override, env merge, deny blocking annotations). ### RC policies (main motivation) This change primarily fixes incorrect SSI behavior when **remote-config policies** are loaded. `IsNamespaceEligible` treated a namespace as “SSI-eligible” if *any* loaded policy *could* match that namespace — even when the policy’s K8s selectors did not match the pod being mutated. In practice, policies that **matched nothing on the pod** (e.g. host/OS-only rules, namespace-scoped rules with pod label constraints, or policies targeting another namespace) could still apply SSI-only mutations in that namespace. Target/policy matching already abstained (no target-selected libraries, no target `ddTraceConfigs`, no `applied-target` / `applied-policy` from a match), but the following **SSI side effects** were still injected whenever the pod was mutated — most visibly on annotation-driven lib injection: - `DD_INSTRUMENTATION_INSTALL_TYPE=k8s_single_step` (instead of `k8s_lib_injection`) - SSI default tracer env vars: `DD_TRACE_ENABLED=true`, `DD_LOGS_INJECTION=true`, `DD_RUNTIME_METRICS_ENABLED=true`, `DD_TRACE_HEALTH_METRICS_ENABLED=true` - UST env vars from pod metadata: `DD_VERSION`, `DD_ENV`, and `DD_SERVICE` (owner/label inference) - SSI-only paths such as language-detection-driven library selection That was a false positive: the pod was not matched by any target or RC policy, but was treated as Single Step Instrumentation anyway. After this PR, RC and local targets use the same predicate for SSI mode as for injection: **did this policy/target match this pod?** ## Behavior changes | Case | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Annotated pod in a namespace that *could* match a rule, but pod does not match (e.g. NS+pod selector) | SSI (`k8s_single_step`, SSI defaults) — **false positive** | `k8s_lib_injection` | | Annotated pod with no matching target/policy | SSI if namespace eligible — **false positive** | `k8s_lib_injection` | | Pod matching a target/policy (with or without annotations) | SSI | SSI (unchanged) | | Annotation + matching target (short-circuit) | SSI if namespace eligible | SSI mode from match; libs/configs still from annotation (unchanged GA selection) | Before: mode was derived from “does any rule match this **namespace**?” — optimistic and non-deterministic for mixed selectors. After: mode is derived from “does any rule match this **pod**?” — same predicate as injection matching. ## Related Issue Follow-up to #54766 ## Type of Change - [ ] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [x] Breaking change - [x] Refactor / cleanup - [ ] CI / tooling - [ ] Documentation ## Checklist - [x] Documentation updated if needed - [x] Tests added or updated - [x] No unintended breaking changes (scoped to SSI mode; selection unchanged) ## How Has This Been Tested? - [x] `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/clusteragent/admission/mutate/autoinstrumentation,./pkg/clusteragent/admission/mutate/common,./pkg/clusteragent/admission/mutate/appsec` - New `ssi_mode_test.go` covers: - annotation-only outside policy scope → lib-injection - mixed NS+pod RC policy → lib-injection when pod labels wrong, SSI when full match - `enabled_namespaces` GA path still SSI on match - annotation short-circuit preserves GA lib selection while mode follows match - Existing `target_matching_test.go` / `rc_policies_test.go` still exercise `getMatchingTarget` ## Additional Notes - Removes dead selector fields from `targetInternal` (matching already delegated to policy engine). - Removes `IsNamespaceEligible` from `MutationFilter` (only `ShouldMutatePod` was used by callers). - DCA release note: `releasenotes-dca/notes/ssi-mode-from-exact-match-cb29a68ef459e96e.yaml`

signal.title: Sort nodes before generating synthetic cluster resourceVersion
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Sorts cluster node information by node name before generating the synthetic cluster resourceVersion. This makes the generated resourceVersion and cluster payload deterministic when the cluster state has not changed. ### Motivation Clusters are synthetic resources and do not have a Kubernetes-provided resourceVersion. The Agent generates one by hashing the serialized cluster payload. Node information originates from an informer-backed map whose iteration order is not deterministic. Consequently, identical cluster states could serialize nodes in different orders and produce different synthetic resource versions. This caused unnecessary cache misses and payload churn. ### Describe how you validated your changes Added a regression test verifying that: * Identical nodes in different orders produce the same synthetic resourceVersion. * An actual change to node information produces a different resourceVersion. * Node information is emitted in canonical order. Also confirmed the regression test fails without the fix and passes with it. The focused race suite passed all 335 tests. ### Additional Notes This complements the backend cache-key changes by stabilizing the Agent-generated synthetic resourceVersion at its source.
signal.author: aureleoules

signal.title: fix(cloudfoundry): avoid nil panic on failed DCA connection
signal.text: ## TL;DR Fixes a nil pointer dereference in the `cloudfoundry-vm` workloadmeta collector that crashes the node Agent on Cloud Foundry when the connection to the Cluster Agent fails. Regressed in 7.81. ## Motivation Agents on Cloud Foundry running 7.81+ panic repeatedly with: ``` panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference clusteragent.(*DCAClient).buildURL(...) clusteragent.go:271 clusteragent.(*DCAClient).GetCFAppsMetadataForNode(0x0, ...) cloudfoundry/vm.(*collector).Pull(...) cf_vm.go:111 ``` Root cause: `getDCAClient()` assigns `clusteragent.GetClusterAgentClient()` (return type `(*DCAClient, error)`) directly into the `c.dcaClient` interface field *before* checking the error. On a failed connection the returned nil `*DCAClient` is boxed into the interface, producing a non-nil "typed nil". The next `Pull` passes the `c.dcaClient != nil` cache check and calls `GetCFAppsMetadataForNode` on the nil receiver, panicking. This became reachable in 7.81 when #50814 changed `GetClusterAgentClient`'s return type from `DCAClientInterface` to `*DCAClient`. Before that, the error path returned a true nil interface, so the field was never poisoned. 7.80.4 is unaffected. ## What this does - `getDCAClient`: assign the result to a local `*DCAClient` and only store it into `c.dcaClient` on success. - `Pull`: call the local `dcaClient` returned by `getDCAClient()` instead of the field `c.dcaClient`. ## Validation / Testing - Added `TestPullDCAConnectionFailureDoesNotPanic`: two `Pull`s with `dcaEnabled=true` and no reachable Cluster Agent; asserts the second does not panic. - Verified the test is a real regression guard: reverting the fix makes it panic at `cf_vm.go:111` (the exact crash line); with the fix all package tests pass. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: Fail fast for real on unusable `XDG_CACHE_HOME` on Windows
signal.text: ### Motivation Accidentally found that a couple of jobs were printing fatal error messages without actually failing fast ([example](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1956102344)) (i.e. continuing past the not-that-fatal error). The problem is that `cmd.exe` happens to zero out the code of an `exit /b <code>` that does not end every enclosing parenthesized block, so `tools/bazel.bat` returned 0 and let subsequent steps to proceed. ### What does this PR do? Reach both fatal diagnostics through `goto` labels placed after the main flow, where `exit /b 2` is now honored. Route the affected jobs through `docker-run-with-bazel-cache.ps1`, as the fixed guards would otherwise fail them, on purpose. ### Describe how you validated your changes On Windows Server 2022 with `bazelisk` 1.28.1, the wrapper returns 2 for an unset and for a relative `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, and still reaches `bazel` for a valid one. `dda inv gitlab.print-ci` shows both jobs inheriting `XDG_CACHE_HOME=c:/bzl`, as `tests_windows-x64` and others already do. ### Additional Notes The two remaining guards do end their blocks, so they already exit 2. Yet another reason for rewriting both `tools/bazel*` hooks in Python.
signal.author: rdesgroppes

signal.title: Pass the lint build tags to --only-modified-packages discovery
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Passes the build tags `golangci-lint` will use to the package discovery done by `dda inv linter.go --only-modified-packages`. ### Motivation `linter.go` passes no build tags, so `process_input_args` turns them into `[]` and `get_modified_packages` skips its `go list` filter (gated on `if build_tags:` since #54890). A modified package whose files are all excluded by the lint tags is then handed to `golangci-lint` as an explicit target, and the run fails with: ``` level=error msg="[linters_context] typechecking error: build constraints exclude all Go files in .../pkg/security/tests/syscall_tester/go" ``` A `./pkg/...` wildcard skips such packages silently, an explicit package name does not, which is why CI (explicit `--targets`, recursive) is unaffected and only the `go-linter` pre-push hook fails. Callers that intentionally pass no tags, such as the Bazel-driven test task, keep skipping the filter. ### Describe how you validated your changes On a branch that modifies `pkg/security/tests/syscall_tester/go`, whose only file is behind `//go:build syscalltesters`: - before: the hook fails with the error above - after: `All linters passed`, and the target list is identical to the one produced before #54890 ### Additional Notes Only affects `--only-modified-packages`, which CI does not use.
signal.author: danielmercier

signal.title: Use subprocess to run bazel commands instead of ctx.run
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? It switches the `bazel` helper to use stdlib `subprocess` to run bazel instead of `ctx.run`. ### Motivation The main motivation for this change is that invoke relies on the stdlib [pty](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pty.html) module for handling the pseudo-terminal, and this library is only available on Unix. The consequence of this is that Bazel's output significantly degrades on Windows, with no color and notably with no rewriting of the output, causing very verbose output that is way harder to read than the default Bazel experience. Switching to `subprocess` sidesteps the need for explicit pty-like handling on Windows (at least as long as we don't want to also capture the output of the command). ### Describe how you validated your changes I ran both `dda inv test` and `dda inv test-new` locally, both on macos and on Windows, and the behavior looks right. And nothing broke in CI. ### Additional Notes This PR attempts to reduce the number of callers modified at once by maintaining the `ctx` argument but not using it. A follow-up PR will remove this argument and fix all callers. The goal was to keep the review for this PR focused on the subprocess handling without having to bring in a bunch of other reviewers. But other changes that affected only a limited number of callers (and which would have require more adaptation code to make work) have been kept as part of this PR. All the extra handling to be able to "tee" the output is targeting the use case from `gotest.py` where output is both meant to be streamed in real time as well as captured for some post-processing logic. This is possibly the most useful feature that invoke was giving us here. In this case, Bazel output will also lose its interactive behavior. However, we're likely to not need this in the near future, once tests are run entirely with Bazel and/or finding other ways to achieve the same.

signal.title: [CWS] Put back subreaper reparenting
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Restores subreaper reparenting support and hardens process cache lineage handling for runtime security. This PR: - Reads live PPid from the kernel process context instead of storing PPid in `pid_cache_t`. - Adds task struct offsets required to read `real_parent->tgid`, including fallback and BTFHub constants. - Removes reverse `Children` links from process cache entries to avoid retaining large stale process subtrees. - Replaces eager child reparenting with lazy direct-edge reparenting from procfs or kernel PPid observations. - Preserves exec chains when reparenting by updating the fork-root edge rather than replacing the current exec head. - Updates PPid only after a successful parent relink. - Adds `StopExecutionTime` so exec replacement time is distinct from final process `ExitTime`. - Marks full same-PID exec chains exited on final exit or PID replacement. - Repairs target process lineage for ptrace tracees and signal/setrlimit targets. - Adds reparenting metrics and callpath tags. - Updates generated model accessors, marshalling/unmarshalling, deep copy handling, docs, and tests. ### Motivation Subreaper reparenting can happen after `do_exit`, which means process lineage observed from eBPF events can temporarily point to an exited parent. The previous approach kept reverse child references in `ProcessCacheEntry`, which made stale lineage expensive and could retain large process trees under high process churn, such as build-cluster workloads. This PR simplifies the cache ownership model by removing reverse child links and repairing lineage lazily when affected processes are observed. It also fixes exec-chain behavior so reparenting does not collapse or corrupt same-PID exec history, and clarifies the difference between an exec replacement and a true process exit. ### Describe how you validated your changes Validation performed: - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/security/resolvers/process` - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/security/probe` - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/security/secl/model` - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/security/seclwin/model` ran with no tests under this configuration. The diff also adds and updates resolver/model tests for subreaper reparenting, lazy repair, exec-chain reparenting, `DequeueExited`, and `StopExecutionTime` behavior.

signal.title: [Backport 7.83.x]  [NETPATH-873] netpath RC feature fix: include config name in netpath payloads
signal.text: Backport f7eb778bcf5c8b68482635889f31f051d20b9140 from #55001. ___ This is a fix for original Network Path via RC introduced in 7.83 Backport motivation: product goal is to release Network Path via RC with 7.73 ### What does this PR do? - Reads `test_config_name` from scheduled and dynamic `NETWORK_PATH` Remote Configuration documents. - Propagates the name alongside `test_config_id` through scheduled checks and dynamic path attribution. - Adds `test_config_name` to Network Path intake payloads when a name is available and verifies it in unit and E2E coverage. - Continues accepting legacy RC documents that do not contain a config name. ### Motivation Network Path configuration names are currently unavailable to the Agent, so emitted traceroute results can identify a configuration only by ID. The corresponding [dd-source change](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/57975) adds the user-facing name to Agent RC content as `test_config_name`. Propagating that value into NetPath payloads lets the backend associate each result with the configuration name while preserving compatibility with configurations created before the rollout. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `bazel test //comp/core/autodiscovery/providers/networkpath:networkpath_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl:impl_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/common:common_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/connfilter:connfilter_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/pathteststore:pathteststore_test //comp/syntheticstestscheduler/impl:impl_test //pkg/collector/corechecks/networkpath:networkpath_test //pkg/networkpath/payload:payload_test` - `bazel build //test/new-e2e/tests/netpath/dynamic-tests:dynamic-tests_test //test/new-e2e/tests/netpath/network-path-integration:network-path-integration_test` ### Additional Notes The Agent intentionally treats `test_config_name` as optional during ingestion so existing stored RC documents remain valid during rollout. Empty names are omitted from emitted payloads, preserving the existing payload shape for legacy and unmanaged producers.

signal.title: fix(ebpf): synchronize perfUsageCollector.Collect with Manager.Start
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes a data race on `PerfMap`/`RingBuffer` telemetry fields: `perfUsageCollector.Collect` reads `BufferSize()` (which reads `bufferSize` without a lock) during Prometheus Gather ticks, while `ebpf.Manager.Start` writes those same fields during eBPF program startup. Changes the collector mutex from `sync.Mutex` to `sync.RWMutex` so `Collect` takes `RLock` (reader), and exports `LockForWrite`/`UnlockForWrite` so `Manager.Start` can take the write lock around `m.Manager.Start()`. ### Motivation Fix a race, found via a race-detector-enabled build in staging (see #54333 for context). ### Describe how you validated your changes Added `TestLockForWriteBlocksCollect` and `TestCollectConcurrentReaders` which validate the lock mechanism: `LockForWrite` blocks `Collect` until `UnlockForWrite` is called, and multiple `Collect` calls can run concurrently under `RLock`. Tests pass under `-race` (`dda inv test --targets=./pkg/ebpf/telemetry/... --race`). The actual race requires eBPF support to trigger (Manager.Start writes to PerfMap/RingBuffer internal fields), so the test validates the synchronization mechanism rather than the full race.
signal.author: pgimalac

signal.title: test(e2e): add IBM MQ integration lab
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a deploy=true E2E-framework lab for the `ibm_mq` integration under `test/e2e-framework/scenarios/aws/integrations/ibm_mq`. The scenario self-provisions **IBM MQ Advanced for Developers 9.3** with a configurable number of queue managers and queues on a single amd64 RHEL 8 EC2 host, co-located with the Datadog Agent. A systemd-driven put/get load generator keeps queue depth and enqueue/dequeue metric families non-zero so the `ibm_mq` check has realistic work to do. It exposes knobs for: - queue-manager count and queues per manager - collection interval - queue selection strategy (auto-discovery / regex / explicit) - `collect_reset_queue_metrics` - metric exclusion patterns - integration and internal profiling Wiring: registered in the integrations `registry.go` + `BUILD.bazel`, and in the invoke task collection, giving the usual task surface: ``` dda inv aws.integrations.ibm-mq.{create,status,check,exec,ssh,destroy,reload-check} ``` ### Motivation Provide a reproducible, self-contained environment to investigate `ibm_mq` check CPU cost as queue-manager and queue counts scale — the check can become expensive with large queue counts and auto-discovery, and this lab makes that behavior easy to reproduce and profile in isolation. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `gofmt` clean on `registry.go` and all `ibm_mq/*.go`. - `go build ./scenarios/aws/integrations/...` in the `test/e2e-framework` module succeeds. - `dda inv aws.integrations -l` lists all `ibm-mq.*` tasks. - pre-commit hooks (shellcheck, go-fmt, copyright, python-linter, …) pass. ### Additional Notes Follows the existing integration-lab pattern (kafka, lustre, etc.). The scenario provisions billable EC2; remember to `dda inv aws.integrations.ibm-mq.destroy` when finished.

signal.title: Titouan.guesdon/clusteragent gomemlimit
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Adds support for `runtime.gomemlimit` in vertical scaling recommendations. When the backend recommendation includes a `Gomemlimit` value for a container, the cluster agent now: 1. Parses `RuntimeValues` (keyed by container name) from the autoscaling backend response 2. Includes `RuntimeValues` in the recommendation hash so changes are detected correctly 3. Injects/updates the `GOMEMLIMIT` environment variable on pods via the admission webhook (`pod_patcher`) 4. Forces a pod rollout (instead of in-place resize) when `RuntimeValues` are present, since env vars cannot be updated on running containers via `pods/resize` 5. Persists `RuntimeValues` to the DPA status annotation so HA follower replicas can reconstruct the full recommendation without hitting the backend ### Motivation Go applications expose a `GOMEMLIMIT` env var to cap the Go runtime's memory usage. Vertical scaling recommendations from the backend can now include this value alongside CPU/memory resource requests/limits, allowing the cluster agent to apply it end-to-end. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit tests in `pod_patcher_test.go` cover: - Injection of `GOMEMLIMIT` when not present - Update of `GOMEMLIMIT` when the value changes - Clearing of `ValueFrom` when the env var was previously sourced from a ConfigMap/Secret (Kubernetes rejects env vars with both `Value` and `ValueFrom` set) ### Additional Notes - `RuntimeValues` are included in the `ResourcesHash` so any change to `GOMEMLIMIT` triggers a new recommendation cycle - Constraints filtering (`applyVerticalConstraints`) also prunes `RuntimeValues` for containers that are dropped, keeping hash consistency
signal.author: TitouanGuesdon

signal.title: fix(system-probe): protect module loader registry with mutex during Register
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes a data race on the module loader registry: `Register` wrote `l.cfg`, `l.stats`, and iterated `l.modules` without holding the loader mutex, racing with `GetStats` which takes the lock. Added `l.Lock()` around the writes and snapshotted module entries before spawning stats goroutines. ### Motivation Fix a race, found via a race-detector-enabled build in staging (see #54333 for context). ### Describe how you validated your changes No unit test added — `Register` requires full eBPF factories, config, and dependencies that can't be constructed in a unit test, and duplicating the internal logic in a test wouldn't validate the actual fix. The race is eliminated by construction: all writes to the shared fields now go through the same mutex that `GetStats` already takes.

signal.title: Prototype: Swinging Door Compression (SDC) streaming compression for check metrics
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Prototypes streaming, bounded-error compression via Swinging Door Trending/Compression (SDC) with an EWMA-smoothed adaptive tolerance, for check metrics, so a check sampled at 1Hz ships full granularity only where the signal actually moves, and collapses to ~1 point per 15s flush window where it's flat. - `pkg/aggregator/internal/sdc`: the core compressor — a single-pass, O(1)-per-sample Swinging Door Trending/Compression implementation with a per-point tolerance (EWMA scale estimate + swing-door segment tracking). Includes a fix for a real correctness gap in the naive swing-door algorithm (a candidate can keep the intersected slope cone non-empty while its own slope already sits outside it, silently misrepresenting an earlier point beyond tolerance) — see the compressor's tests and comments for the concrete counterexample. - `pkg/aggregator/sender/sdcsender`: a `SenderManager`/`Sender` decorator that applies the compressor to `Gauge`/`Count`/`Rate`/`MonotonicCount`/`GaugeWithTimestamp`/`CountWithTimestamp` calls, selected per check name at `loader.Load()` time (`pkg/collector/scheduler.go`). This works for any check loader (Go, Python, ...) since every loader reaches the aggregator exclusively through this same interface — no changes to `CheckSampler` or the aggregator core. `Rate`/`MonotonicCount` replicate their delta/reset-detection logic locally, since the `Sender` interface carries no timestamp for the real aggregator-side state to hook into. - Telemetry (`sdcsender_samples_total` / `sdcsender_breakpoints_total`, tagged by metric name) makes the per-metric compression ratio observable directly. - A dry-run mode (`checks.sdc_compression_dry_run`) runs every sample through the compressor for measurement, but ships the check's original, uncompressed calls — useful for evaluating what compression would do before turning it on for real. ### Motivation Checks currently emit at a fixed interval (typically 15s), which is a fixed trade-off between granularity and volume for every signal shape. This prototype explores sampling faster (1Hz) and letting a bounded-error compressor decide, per metric, how many points are actually needed to reconstruct the signal within tolerance — full resolution for spikes/steps, minimal for flat/smooth signals. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `pkg/aggregator/internal/sdc`: unit tests assert the bounded-error property across synthetic signals (flat, ramp, spikes, step, near-zero jitter, random walk) and a dedicated regression test for the swing-door correctness fix. - `pkg/aggregator/sender/sdcsender`: unit tests cover compression routing per metric kind, spike/flat/window-boundary behavior, Rate derivative computation, MonotonicCount reset detection, tag-order independence, dry-run forwarding, and pass-through of unintercepted `Sender` methods. - End-to-end, live: built a custom agent and ran it against a local Docker Compose testbench (real agent + fakeintake) with a scripted OpenMetrics endpoint serving a flat signal, a step, a spike, and a monotonic counter. Verified via `fakeintake` that: - the flat signal and the monotonic counter (whose per-scrape delta is constant) both compress to ~1 point per 15s window, - the step and spike signals ship extra points exactly at their real transitions, - dry-run mode ships the exact same uncompressed points as with `sdcsender` absent, while `samples_total`/`breakpoints_total` still show the would-be compression ratio (e.g. ~10:1 for the flat signal). ### Additional Notes This is a prototype/experiment, not production-ready: - The check-name allowlist (`checks.sdc_compression_checks`) and compressor parameters (epsilon/alpha/floor) are placeholders pending real-world tuning. - The real (Python) `openmetrics` check itself hasn't been exercised end-to-end in this sandbox (no Python/rtloader support here); the throwaway `vbrscrapeprobe` stand-in check used earlier for that verification has since been removed now that manual verification against a real agent covered the same `Sender` interface path. - Backend/staging interpretation of the resulting irregular-timestamp series (rollups, graphing) hasn't been verified. Renamed from the internal "VBR" (variable bit rate) codename to "SDC" (Swinging Door Compression) throughout, since that's the actual, well-known algorithm this implements.

signal.title: [CONTINT-5277] Wait for workloadmeta before running `agent check`
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes `agent check <name>` wait for the workloadmeta store to report itself as initialized before running the check, bounded by a new `--workloadmeta-timeout` flag (40s by default, `0` to disable). `process-agent check` already had a private copy of that wait loop, so the helper lands in a new `pkg/util/workloadmeta` package and both commands share it. `cluster-agent check` gets the behavior too, since it is built from the same `pkg/cli/subcommands/check`. ### Motivation `agent check` runs in its own short-lived process and builds **its own** in-process workloadmeta store with the full collector catalog (`cmd/agent/subcommands/check/command.go` injects `wmcatalog.GetCatalog()`). Collectors are started asynchronously — the store only becomes usable after `firstCollectorReady` (or its own 30s `firstPullWaitTimeout`) — but the command never waited for them: it resolved configs (`--discovery-timeout`, 5s, instant for the file-provided `container` config) and ran the check right away. When the store is still empty, `generic.Processor.run` returns early **without an error** (`pkg/collector/corechecks/containers/generic/processor.go:80-84`), so the check reports `Metric Samples: Total: 0` and no failure. That is a real product bug — `agent check container` in a pod can silently print nothing — and it is the top remaining flake of the `new-e2e-containers` jobs. Typical failing output: ``` Total Runs: 3 Metric Samples: Last Run: 0, Total: 0 Average Execution Time: 0s ERROR (autoconfig.go:179) Workloadmeta collectors are not ready after 2 retries: backoff: maximum elapsed time exceeded (last error: workloadmeta not initialized) --- FAIL: TestKindSuite/TestCLI/agent_CLI/agent_check_-r_container (120.01s) ``` The e2e assertion retries for 2 minutes, but every tick spawns a fresh process that pays the same cold start, so the failure is deterministic at 120s. Over Aug 6 → Aug 14 on `main` this single sub-test accounts for ~61 job failures, spread evenly over the six `TestKindSuite` matrix variants (1.19, 1.22, 1.27, 1.29, ubuntu 20-04, ubuntu 22-04) plus `new-e2e-containers-k8s-latest`. It is absent from EKS, where the node is not a single kind VM. A useful contrast: the neighbouring `agent workload-list` sub-test almost never fails, because it queries the **running** agent over IPC instead of starting its own store. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `go test -tags=test` on `pkg/util/workloadmeta`, `pkg/cli/subcommands/check` and `pkg/cli/subcommands/processchecks` — the new package has unit tests for the already-ready, becomes-ready-while-polling, timeout, disabled and cancelled-context paths. - `go build` of the affected packages with and without container build tags (`docker containerd cri kubelet kubeapiserver orchestrator zlib zstd`). - The real validation is CI: the `new-e2e-containers` matrix. After merge, the number to watch is the failure count of `@test.name:"TestKindSuite/TestCLI/agent_CLI/agent_check_-r_container"` on `main` (reference: ~61 over 8 days) and the overall failure rate of `new-e2e-containers*` jobs (reference: 6.3%, down from 16.7% before the `http_status_code` fix in #54313). ### Additional Notes Scope and known limits, stated explicitly: - `IsInitialized()` is workloadmeta's **best-effort** readiness signal — the store reports itself initialized once at least one collector has started (`store.go:771`, not all of them) and the first pull round has been *kicked off*, not completed. This closes the multi-second startup race that produces the failures above; it does not make the race impossible. The code comments and the release note are deliberately worded that way. - Two follow-ups for the workloadmeta owners, not done here: - `comp/core/autodiscovery/impl/autoconfig.go:158-181` hand-rolls the same `IsInitialized()` poll and could use this helper, but that changes the running agent's autodiscovery startup timing. - `store.go:712-717` returns before `startCandidates` sets `CollectorsStarting`, so an **empty** collector catalog would leave `IsInitialized()` false forever. Not reachable for the commands touched here (`catalog-core` always contains the untagged CloudFoundry collectors, and `catalog-clusteragent`'s kubeapiserver collector is present whenever the DCA `check` command is compiled), but it is a latent trap. - **`--workloadmeta-timeout` is when to give up, not a hard bound on how long the command blocks.** Probing the store takes `collectorMut` (`store.go:672-675`), which `startCandidates` holds across every collector's `Start` (`store.go:749-750`), and `Start` does unbounded-in-aggregate work (image and container listing with a per-item inspect). A probe can therefore return after the deadline, and the state it found is then reported rather than discarded. This is intended: giving up on the deadline would mean running the check against a store whose collectors are still starting, i.e. reproducing the very empty-output failure this PR removes. Returning the right data late beats returning nothing on time here, since nothing downstream imposes that deadline and the command is interruptible. Raised as P2 by Codex and P1 by Datadog Autotest; both threads have the full reasoning. - After `firstPullWaitTimeout` the store reports itself initialized even if no collector ever started, in which case the wait returns success and no warning is emitted — the silent-empty-output case survives on that path only. - The timeout warning goes to stderr, never stdout, and is suppressed in `--json` mode: some e2e host executors merge the two streams and parse the result as JSON. - A separate change will align `new-e2e-containers` on `.retry_only_infra_failure` like the EKS/OpenShift jobs, once this fix is confirmed effective on `main` — doing it before would trade costly retries for red `main` builds. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: feat(autodiscovery): tag configuration-discovery instances to mitigate duplicate metrics risk (#54660)
signal.text: Adds a `dd_config_discovery:true` tag to every check instance scheduled via the Autodiscovery configuration-discovery mechanism (i.e. any `auto_conf.yaml` template with `discovery: {}`, resolved through `comp/core/autodiscovery/impl/configmgr_discovery.go`'s `applyDiscoveredConfigsLocked`). The tag used is `dd_config_discovery:true`, a plain `dd_`-prefixed key, following the precedent of other agent-added, customer-visible marker/provenance tags already in the codebase: - `dd_remote_config_id` / `dd_remote_config_rev` (`comp/core/tagger/tags/tags.go`) - `dd_enable_check_intake` (`pkg/collector/worker/worker.go`) [DSCVR-651](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/DSCVR-651): there is a risk that an agent on host A is monitoring a service on host B with a manually-configured check (e.g. a generic `openmetrics` check), while the agent running locally on host B also autodiscovers and schedules a dedicated integration for the same service via configuration discovery. Neither agent's local anti-duplication logic can see the other's config, so both submit metrics for the same underlying data. This tag doesn't prevent the duplication, but lets users identify and, if needed, exclude the autodiscovered side of it (e.g. `metric{!dd_config_discovery:true}`), both for the cross-host case above and for any single-host case the automatic suppression doesn't catch. Unit and E2E tests. --- 🤖 This PR description and implementation were generated with assistance from [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code). signal.title: [WINA-3031] Upgrade datadog-go to v5.9.1
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? - Upgrades `github.com/DataDog/datadog-go/v5` from `v5.9.0` to `v5.9.1` across the Go workspace. ### Motivation [#incident-59243](https://dd.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C0BQAB1T274) https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3031 `datadog-go v5.9.1` fixes a nil pointer dereference in the Windows named-pipe writer (DataDog/datadog-go#397). The pipe connection is established on first write, so closing a client that never successfully wrote dereferenced a nil `net.Conn` and terminated the process. The Agent Data Plane pre-flight probe triggers this on Windows. It dials the pipe once to prove readiness, then the statsd client dials again on its first write; when that second dial loses a startup race, the deferred `client.Close()` crashed the Agent service with `0xc0000005`. This is intermittent by nature — it needs the first dial to succeed and the second to fail. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `go list -m github.com/DataDog/datadog-go/v5` resolves to `v5.9.1`. - `go mod verify` — all modules verified. - `GOOS=windows go build ./comp/dataplane/...` passes. The fix is in a `//go:build windows` file, so a native build would not exercise it. - Confirmed every changed `go.mod`/`go.sum` line is datadog-go and nothing else. ### Additional Notes Renovate normally owns this bump (it did v5.9.0 in #53234), but `minimumReleaseAge: 7 days` means it would not open a PR until ~2026-08-24. Landing it manually since the crash blocks 7.84. The diff matches Renovate's output file-for-file, so it will simply see the dependency as current.

signal.title: [SBOM] Skip images whose SBOM cannot be uncompressed
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? processImageSBOM logged the error from UncompressSBOM and carried on, but UncompressSBOM returns no SBOM alongside its error, so reading its status a few lines later dereferenced a nil pointer. The check worker recovers from a panic in Run, so that one misbehaving check cannot take the process with it, but the long-running check wrapper returns from Run as soon as it has started the goroutine the check really runs on, and the recover never covers that goroutine. An image whose stored SBOM cannot be uncompressed therefore brings the whole Agent down, and does so again at every refresh for as long as workloadmeta holds it. Skip the image instead. It is reported again once it is scanned anew.

signal.title: [SBOM] Refresh every image when spreading the refresh
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? The spread refresher divides the image count by the number of steps it spreads a period over to decide how many images to refresh per step. The division truncates, so a host with fewer than ten images refreshed none of them, ever. An image SBOM was then sent only when the image changed or when a container first ran it, so inUse stayed true after the last container stopped. Above ten, unless the count was a multiple of ten, the refresh was merely slower than configured. Fifteen images took one and a half periods to cycle. Round the count up. Every image is then covered within one period, at the cost of at most nine extra refreshes per period. That overhead only matters where images are few, and a host with a single image now sends it once per step rather than once per period. The refresher is off by default, so this only affects hosts that set sbom.container_image.use_spread_refresher.

signal.title: Reject unresolved secret handles on the NPM direct-send path
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds `endpoint.CheckAPIKeysResolved` and calls it from `sender.New` (`pkg/network/sender/sender_linux.go`), so that when `network_config.direct_send` is enabled and `api_key` is still an unresolved `ENC[...]` secret handle, the NPM direct sender refuses to start and says why: ``` error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ("ENC[...]"): this process does not resolve secret-backend handles, provide the api_key as a plain value or enable config sync from the core agent (agent_ipc.config_refresh_interval) ``` The check also covers `process_config.additional_endpoints`, since those keys come from the same config and are equally likely to be secret-backed. ### Motivation NTWK-817. A customer set `api_key` via the secret backend (`ENC[k8s_secret@...]`) and enabled `network_config.direct_send`. CNM data never arrived, and nothing in the logs pointed at the cause. What was happening: system-probe wires the **no-op** secrets component (`secretsnoopfx.Module()` in `cmd/system-probe/subcommands/run/command.go`), so it cannot resolve secret handles itself. It only ever receives resolved values from the core agent over config sync (`comp/core/configsync`)— both `agent_ipc.config_refresh_interval` and `agent_ipc.port` default to `0` (`pkg/config/setup/all_settings.go`). With config sync off, `config.GetString("api_key")` returned the literal string `ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, and the direct sender passed it straight through as the `Dd-Api-Key` header. Every payload was rejected by the intake, and because the direct sender has no API-key validation (`DisableAPIKeyChecking = true`) there was no error identifying the key as the problem. Silent data loss. This does not make the customer's setup work — it makes the failure legible. The configuration they still need is in the section below. ### Scope of the check, and why it is not in `GetAPIEndpoints` The check is deliberately **not** inside `GetAPIEndpoints`, even though that is where the API key is read. `module.FactoryDependencies` (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/common.go`) declares `ConnectionsForwarder connectionsforwarder.Component` as a **non-optional** field, and `startSystemProbe` takes that struct — so Fx constructs `connectionsforwarder` on **every** system-probe start regardless of `direct_send`, and its constructor calls `GetAPIEndpoints` and propagates the error (`comp/forwarder/connectionsforwarder/impl/connectionsforwarder.go`). Putting the check there made any system-probe with a secret-backed `api_key` fail to boot outright, taking CWS, USM, and discovery with it — a regression for a large existing population, since that construction was previously a harmless no-op (a forwarder built with an unusable key that nothing read). Keeping the check at the `sender.New` call site means the failure is confined to what is actually broken: the module loader logs the error and skips `network_tracer`, and the rest of system-probe runs normally (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/loader.go`). NPM and USM are both lost, as they share the `network_tracer` module — unavoidable without silently falling back to the process-agent collection path, which would change the deployment topology in response to a config error. Graceful degradation was considered and rejected. `Register()` skips the `/connections` endpoint when `DirectSend` is true, so keeping the module alive without a sender would load eBPF programs, collect connections, and drop them all — the cost of NPM with none of the data, and quietly. ### Customer-facing configuration required for `direct_send` + secrets To make secret-backed `api_key` actually work with `direct_send`, config sync must be enabled so the core agent supplies the resolved value. In `datadog.yaml` (read by both the core agent and system-probe), either TCP: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 # seconds; must be > 0 port: 5008 # any free port ``` or, preferably in Kubernetes, over a socket: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 use_socket: true socket_path: /var/run/datadog/agent_ipc.socket # on a volume both containers mount ``` One of the two transports must be set. `comp/core/configsync/impl/module.go` logs `configsync disabled: ...` and does nothing if `config_refresh_interval <= 0`, or if `use_socket` is false and `port <= 0`. Caveats worth flagging to anyone enabling this: - **Startup becomes dependent on core-agent readiness.** system-probe runs config sync with `OnInitSync: true` and a **10-second** deadline (`configSyncTimeout`, retrying every 2s). If the core agent is not yet listening, system-probe fails to start with `failed to sync config at startup, is the core agent listening on '...'`. Where both start together this is a real race. - **`use_socket` needs a shared volume.** The standard Helm chart does not give the two containers a shared writable run directory by default; an explicit `emptyDir` mounted into both is required. - The only alternative is a literal `api_key` in the config system-probe reads, which defeats the point of using a secret backend. This interaction is currently undocumented — `direct_send` has no entry in `pkg/config/example/system-probe_*.yaml.example`, no description in the generated schema, and no coverage under `docs/`. Documentation is intentionally left out of this PR and will be handled separately. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit: added `endpoints_test.go` covering a plain key, a bare handle, a whitespace-padded handle, a handle in an additional endpoint, and an empty key. `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/process/runner/endpoint` passes; `dda inv linter.go` clean on `pkg/process/runner/endpoint` and `pkg/network/sender`. End-to-end, in a Linux container (arm64, kernel 6.8, CO-RE) with `direct_send: true`, `api_key: ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, `process_config.process_dd_url` pointed at a local stub intake, and no config sync configured: | | before this change | with this change | |---|---|---| | system-probe process | runs but direct sender gets payloads rejected | stays up, socket bound | | `network_tracer` | n/a | `error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ...` | | other modules | none | `discovery` and `event_monitor` both started | | requests reaching intake | payloads sent with `Dd-Api-Key: ENC[...]` | 0 | | `ENC[` observed on the wire | yes | 0 | `dda inv system-probe.build` also verified in the Linux container, since `sender_linux.go` is not compiled on macOS. ### Additional Notes The error message names the offending setting path, so it distinguishes `api_key` from `process_config.additional_endpoints`. The handle itself is included in the message; it is a reference, not a secret value.
